## Context

See proposal.md for motivation, and
[docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md)
for the measurements every decision below rests on — taken live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the
e2e harness, then reviewed by hand in a demo build whose two experimental settings this change
removes.

Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:

1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on
   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.
2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
   quantum that is not the Tab size.
3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
  one of ours.

**Non-Goals:**

- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
  three-space indentation). See Risks.
- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.

## Decisions

### D1 — Set the variables Obsidian reads, rather than positioning list lines ourselves

Scope `--list-indent` (and the guide and marker-gap variables) to `.cm-line.to-decor-list`, the
class the decoration already puts on list-item lines. Both gates — outline mode, and lists only
— then come from the decoration itself and the CSS needs no second condition. Confirmed live:
an outline-mode note retargets and a non-outline note open beside it is byte-identical to
stock.

*Alternatives considered.* Measuring each item's bullet and drawing overlays at those
coordinates (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) was the approach two earlier
probes concluded was the only one available. It is a second rendering mechanism with its own
reflow bookkeeping, and Experiment 2b replaced exactly that with the measurement-free gradient
the layer now rests on. Forcing a width onto `.cm-hmd-list-indent` per line was also built and
measured: the geometry is right and the caret round-trips, but it desynchronises Obsidian's
hanging indent (see D3) and needs a per-line custom property where a single variable does.

### D2 — Draw the list guides ourselves; do not share with Obsidian's

Suppress the native indent guide on our list lines (its width, not the user's setting, so the
`.cm-indent` spans that carry layout still exist) and lift `computeLineGuides`' list-item
exclusion so the existing gradient draws every level.

Keeping the native guide was the cheaper option and was rejected on two measured grounds. It
disappears entirely when the user turns "Show indentation guides" off, so list levels would
lose their guides for a reason unrelated to outline mode. And it accents only ONE level — the
caret's own, via `.cm-active-indent` — where the trail accents the whole ancestor chain, so the
position indicator would still be missing inside lists, which is one of the things this change
exists to fix.

`LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths in a field of their own rather than
merged into `guideDepths`. The walk publishes them unconditionally and the consumer combines
them, which keeps the fact independent of any rendering decision and keeps the per-`Text`
fact cache correct without a second key.

### D3 — State the hanging indent; do not read Obsidian's

Write `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent` on our list lines from
`(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter`, with `!important` — the rule this codebase
already relies on for `to-decor-block`, where an important stylesheet declaration beats
Obsidian's non-important inline style.

Two measured defects close together. Obsidian derives the hang from `coordsAtPos` at the end of
the marker, which reports the end of the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box:
with the marker span sized to the gutter, every soft-wrapped list row lands 16px left of its
own item's text (measured 100.0 against a text column of 116.0). And because the value is
cached against attributes the observer does not watch, retargeting the grid at runtime — which
is what turning outline mode on does — leaves the old value in place until the note is
reopened. A stated value has neither problem: measured exact in both the freshly-opened and
the toggled-on case.

*Alternative considered and rejected.* Provoking the `childList` mutation Obsidian's cache does
watch (append an empty hidden span to each list line, remove it again) was built and confirmed
to work, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. It was backed out: this repo's own
lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU
mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a
judgement rather than a measurement. Stating the value removes the need entirely.

### D4 — The bullet is Obsidian's, positioned and weighted by us

Keep the native `.list-bullet` rather than replacing it with a synthetic marker. It is already
a real element on the real column, it already carries the collapsed/hover states and the
accent hooks `hierarchy-position-indicators` uses, and its appearance is entirely
variable-driven (`--list-bullet-size`, `-radius`, `-border`, `-transform`,
`--list-marker-color`) — so customisable bullets later are a settings surface over variables,
not new geometry.

Position: zero `--list-padding-inline-start`, a zero-width bullet box so its absolutely
positioned dot centres on the box's own start edge, and the whole marker span sized to the
marker gutter with `min-width`. Sizing the SPAN rather than padding the glyph is what makes the
text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction rather than the sum of a
padding, a glyph and a space.

Weight: `--list-bullet-size: 0.38em`, colour token unchanged. Screenshotted at 0.30 (Obsidian's
default, 4.8px), 0.38, 0.45em and at `--text-muted`; 0.38em at the shared `--text-faint` lands
at the block icons' ink weight, 0.45em reads large against the text, and `--text-muted` makes
the bullet heavier than the markers it is matching.

### D5 — Ordered markers start on the column; task checkboxes keep native geometry

`min-width`, not `width`, on the marker span: a bullet gets exactly the gutter and a wide
ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own text out rather than overlapping it. Ordered markers
therefore START on the column instead of centring on it, and an item numbered past 9 starts its
text slightly further right than its siblings. Right-aligning numbers into the gutter would
read better but needs a wrapper element the DOM does not provide.

Task lines are excluded from the marker-column rule: the checkbox lives in the same span, is
wider than the gutter, and is a real click target whose hit area should not be reshaped in
passing. Both are recorded as follow-ups rather than solved here.

### D6 — One column definition, shared by markers, guides and accents

Measured: a marker's centre sits at exactly `depth × unit`, while a guide paints its 1px as
`[column, column + 1]`, so its visible centre is `column + 0.5` — every marker in the layer,
bullets and block icons alike, is half a pixel left of its own guide. Separately, a bullet
centres on its text rect's geometric centre while a block icon sits about 5px above it, so the
two kinds do not share a vertical rule.

Both are resolved by making the column — horizontal and vertical — one value that the guide
gradient, the marker offset and the accent layers all derive from, rather than three call sites
that agree by convention. This is the standing rule doc 11 draws from Experiment 5b's three
near-identical bugs: when two things must move together, make it impossible to change one
without the other.

### D7 — Remove the settings

The demo build's `listLayout` and `listBullet` dropdowns and their persisted fields go. They
existed to make the comparison possible, the comparison happened, and keeping them would mean
committing to four rendering combinations. Existing `data.json` files carrying the fields are
simply ignored — the plugin reads its data through defaults and writes back only known keys.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- **Two- and three-space indented files stay misaligned, and more visibly than before.**
  Obsidian resolves only a tab or exactly four spaces into an indent unit, so those files
  render their levels at literal whitespace widths — with the plugin disabled too. Once our
  guides sit on an even grid, bullets that do not is a visible mismatch rather than a merely
  uneven one. → Verify against a real two-space file and document it in the settings/readme
  surface; the durable fix is a normalize-indentation command, out of scope here.
- **Space-indented files depend on a setting the user owns.** With "Show indentation guides"
  off, the `.cm-indent` spans do not exist and four-space levels collapse to natural width.
  Tab-indented files are unaffected (`tab-size` is independent of it). → Detect and surface
  rather than silently render wrong; decide the surface during implementation.
- **We now override native list chrome, the surface the original postmortem blames for most of
  the earlier failure.** → The overrides are variables Obsidian itself exposes plus one stated
  hang, not a fight with its box model; every one is verified by measurement and by a
  screenshot pass, and the additive-only discipline still holds for every non-list kind.
- **Theme collision.** A theme that sets `--list-indent` itself (Minimal does, at `2em`, via
  Style Settings) loses that setting inside outline mode; Minimal additionally puts its own
  `--list-edit-offset` margin on list lines, which our own `margin-left !important` replaces.
  → Include Minimal in the manual pass, as `docs/research/12`'s existing Minimal entry
  requires.
- **Three existing trail tests assert the behaviour being removed** ("runs the segment at the
  shallower non-list column, through the list levels", "accents only the non-list ancestor in
  the guides style", "draws no segment anywhere in a pure list, in either style"). → They are
  the regression net for the old contract and are rewritten against the new one, not deleted
  quietly.
- **Obsidian could change any of this.** The variables are identical in 1.12.7 and 1.13.4, and
  `--list-indent`/`--list-spacing`/`--list-marker-color` are documented; the guide and bullet
  variables are not. → Every value we set has a working fallback, and the e2e suite measures
  rendered geometry rather than asserting the variables exist.

## Open Questions

- What the surface should be when a note's list indentation cannot render on the grid (a
  two-space file, or a space-indented file with indent guides off): a one-time notice, a
  status-bar hint, nothing but documentation. It changes no requirement and no task boundary,
  so it can be settled while implementing the verification pass.

      and the gradient's 1px stop all derive from it, so a marker's visible centre and its
      guide's visible centre coincide by construction rather than by convention. Fix the
      measured half-pixel: markers sit at `depth × unit`, the guide paints `[column, column+1]`.
- [ ] 1.2 Establish one vertical anchor for markers across kinds — measured today, a bullet
      centres on its text rect while a block icon sits ~5px above it. Decide the anchor against
      the optical centre of a text row (a rect centre reads ~1.5px high), apply it to synthetic
      markers and the native bullet alike, and fold in `docs/research/12`'s existing
      "vertical-alignment polish" entry for the widget-atom icons while the rule is being set.
- [ ] 1.3 Declare `--to-decor-unit` as a real value rather than a CSS fallback, so
      `--list-indent` and everything else read one number. No user setting in this change.
- [ ] 1.4 Unit-test the shared derivation; e2e-assert that a block marker's centre, a bullet's
      centre and their guide's centre agree at the same depth, in both bundled themes.

      emitted unconditionally (content lines and gap lines alike) so a blank line inside a list
      keeps its guides continuous. Already present on the demo branch — review it against the
      spec rather than rewriting it.

      paragraph, a multi-line item's continuation, a gap line between items, and a non-list
      child of a list item.
- [ ] 2.3 Remove `computePositionTrail`'s two `isListItem` exclusions (`'full'`'s `continue`,
      `'lineage'`'s rung filter) so the trail steps one level per ancestor whatever its kind.
- [ ] 2.4 Rewrite the three trail tests that assert the old omission — "runs the segment at the
      shallower non-list column, through the list levels", "accents only the non-list ancestor
      in the guides style", "draws no segment anywhere in a pure list, in either style" —
      against the new contract, and add a pure-list lineage case.

      state the hanging indent.

p = 'openspec/changes/lists-on-the-outline-grid/specs/outline-decorations/spec.md'
s = open(p).read()

# 1. The indentation requirement: its NAME asserts what the change reverses, so replace
#    the whole requirement rather than modify it under a now-false name.
old_start = s.index("### Requirement: Additive-only indentation, native list rendering untouched")
old_end = s.index("### Requirement: Indentation guides render every ancestor level, including list levels")
old_block = s[old_start:old_end]
s = s[:old_start] + s[old_end:]

added_block = """### Requirement: Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid
Every node's lines SHALL carry an indentation contribution equal to `depth × unit`,
computed from the node's distance from the document root in the parsed tree — not from raw
markdown indentation or heading level. Which CSS property carries that contribution SHALL be
determined by the line's RENDERED FORM, not by its node's kind: a line rendered as plain
text with no visible box of its own takes it as `padding-left`; a line that renders a
visible box of its own — an atom, or any line Obsidian replaces with an opaque widget —
takes it as `margin-left`, since padding does not move a visible box's own edges.

A LIST ITEM takes its contribution in two parts, which together put it on that same grid:
`supplementalDepth × unit` as `margin-left`, where `supplementalDepth` is the count of
non-list-item ancestors above the nearest list root, plus the item's own depth WITHIN its
list, which Obsidian's own list rendering supplies once the outline unit is the unit it
renders a list level at. The plugin SHALL retarget that native rendering by supplying the
unit, and SHALL state the item's own hanging indent; it SHALL NOT reposition a list item by
overriding native rendering line by line.

Nodes at the same tree depth SHALL receive the same indentation contribution regardless of
whether their depth is encoded via heading level, list indentation, or paragraph adjacency,
AND regardless of whether the line is currently rendered as plain text or as an opaque widget.

#### Scenario: Heading and list depth align
- **WHEN** a `### Heading` two tree-levels deep (nested under an `#` and a `##` ancestor)
  and a twice-indented list item are both visible in the same document
- **THEN** both render the same indentation contribution

#### Scenario: A list shifts as a whole under a non-list ancestor, and steps by the unit within itself
- **WHEN** a list sits under a heading
- **THEN** the list's start position shifts right by the heading's own depth contribution,
  and each of its own nesting levels is one unit from the last — the same unit the heading
  levels use

#### Scenario: Multiline continuation lines match their node's first line
- **WHEN** a paragraph or list item spans multiple physical lines (via a hard line break)
- **THEN** every continuation line carries the same indentation contribution as the node's
  first line

#### Scenario: A widget-rendered line aligns with its same-depth plain siblings
- **WHEN** a line whose node is NOT an atom (e.g. a paragraph consisting of a note embed,
  `![[Another note]]`) is rendered by Obsidian as an opaque replacement element, and a plain
  paragraph sits at the same tree depth in the same document
- **THEN** both start at the same column — the widget-rendered line's indentation
  contribution is its node's, exactly as though it had rendered as plain text

"""
# insert the replacement into the ADDED section, before the hanging-indent requirement
anchor = "### Requirement: A list item's hanging indent is stated, not measured"
s = s.replace(anchor, added_block + anchor, 1)

# 2. Keep the marker scenario's existing name; scope it to what is genuinely unchanged.
old_sc = """#### Scenario: List items keep their native marker at every setting
- **WHEN** a list item is rendered in outline mode, at any `markerVisibility` setting
- **THEN** it shows Obsidian's own bullet or number, positioned and weighted by this layer,
  with no additional synthetic marker"""
new_sc = """#### Scenario: List items are unchanged
- **WHEN** a list item is rendered in outline mode, at any `markerVisibility` setting
- **THEN** `markerVisibility` changes nothing about it: no synthetic marker is ever added,
  and its native bullet or number is never hidden

#### Scenario: A native bullet carries a marker's weight
- **WHEN** a list item and a paragraph are visible in the same document
- **THEN** the bullet reads at a comparable visual weight to the paragraph's marker, and both
  resolve their colour from the same token"""
assert old_sc in s
s = s.replace(old_sc, new_sc)

# 3. Record the removal of the old indentation requirement.
removal = """
### Requirement: Additive-only indentation, native list rendering untouched

**Reason**: The requirement's own name states the constraint this change reverses — it
required that a list item's native `text-indent`/`padding-left` hang pair never be modified
and that list rendering be left entirely to Obsidian, which is what kept list levels off the
outline grid and their guides on columns no other kind uses.

**Migration**: Replaced by "Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid",
which keeps every scenario and every rule about non-list kinds verbatim and states how a list
item reaches the same grid: the unit is supplied to Obsidian's own list rendering and the
hanging indent is stated rather than measured. Additive-only still describes the non-list
kinds exactly as before.
"""
s = s.rstrip() + "\n" + removal
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

docs(research): how Obsidian computes list geometry, and what we can own

Measurement pass for the parking lot's "native list decoration experiments"
entry, answering whether list rendering can be brought up to the level of the
heading/paragraph/atom layer.

Two earlier probes (docs/research/14, finding 3) concluded that native list
columns could only be FOLLOWED, by per-item pixel measurement — a second
rendering mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient the whole layer
rests on. That conclusion was right about the mechanism it examined and wrong
about the problem: Obsidian computes list columns from public CSS variables, so
they can be SET instead.

Measured live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the e2e harness:

- `--list-indent` (documented) drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width`
  on each `.cm-indent`; pushing our own unit into it retargets every tab- or
  four-space-indented level at once, and Obsidian's hanging indent re-derives
  itself.
- `--indentation-guide-editing-indent: -1px` puts the native list guides on our
  own guide columns exactly. The -1px is not a nudge: Obsidian paints its guide
  as `border-inline-end` on a 1px-wide pseudo-element, so a 0 offset lands one
  pixel right of the column.
- Scoping to our own per-line class works; a note without outline mode open at
  the same time is byte-identical to stock.
- `.cm-indent` spans exist only while "Show indentation guides" is on, and one
  is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — so two- and three-space files
  are misaligned in stock Obsidian, and space-indented files depend on that
  setting for their layout.
- The hanging indent is a cached live measurement whose invalidation watches
  childList/characterData/subtree but not attributes.
- A marker's centre sits at `depth × unit` while a guide paints
  `[column, column+1]`, so every marker — bullets and block icons alike — is
  half a pixel left of its own guide. Bullets and block icons also use
  different vertical anchors.

Also records what the numbers did not say: a column measured to the right value
can still be drawn a pixel off it, and two things on the same column are not the
same as two things in the same relationship.

Cross-links the parking lot entries this supersedes: the deferred trail-along-
native-list-columns item, the "shrinking only our own added list margin"
question, and the bullet-style half of layer configurability.

Puts list decoration on the same grid as everything else outline mode draws.

Today a document in outline mode has two layouts in it. Headings, paragraphs and atoms sit on a depth column every `--to-decor-unit`, with a marker centred on that column and a guide descending from it. Lists are handed back to Obsidian: a list level steps `2.25em` where every other level steps `1.5rem`, its guides sit on native columns our grid never touches, and a list ancestor gets no caret trail at all because there is no column of ours to draw one on.

The experiment series left it that way deliberately, and two later probes concluded native list columns could only be *followed*, by per-item pixel measurement — a second rendering mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient the layer rests on. That was right about the mechanism it examined and wrong about the problem. Obsidian computes list columns from public CSS variables, so they can be **set**. `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` measures the whole surface against a running Obsidian 1.13.4; a demo build of it was reviewed by hand and accepted.

## What the change does

- **One indentation grid for every kind.** `--to-decor-unit` is pushed into Obsidian's own `--list-indent` on outline-mode list lines, so a list level and a heading level are the same distance.
- **Our own guides draw every list level**, in the same gradient, colour and column a heading's guide uses. Obsidian's own list guide is suppressed on those lines — its width, never the user's "Show indentation guides" setting.
- **The caret trail reaches into lists.** With list levels on the grid, `computePositionTrail`'s two `isListItem` exclusions come out and the position indicator accents list levels like any other. This closes the omission `hierarchy-position-indicators` currently states as a requirement.
- **A list marker sits on its own depth column**, with the item's text at the marker gutter, so a guide descends *out of* its bullet rather than beside it.
- **We state the hanging indent instead of reading Obsidian's.** Measured: the marker gutter makes every soft-wrapped list row land 16px left of its own item's text, because `coordsAtPos` — and therefore Obsidian's own measurement — reports the end of the marker's *text*, not the end of its padded box. Writing the pair from `(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter` is exact, and being a `calc()` it also removes the stale-cache defect where retargeting the grid at runtime left the old wrap column in place.
- **The bullet gets a marker's weight**: `--list-bullet-size: 0.38em`, colour token unchanged so lists and blocks retune together. Bullet appearance stays entirely variable-driven, which is what makes customisable bullets later a settings surface rather than new geometry.
- **Markers and guides share one column definition.** Measured: every marker's centre sits at exactly `depth × unit` while a guide paints its 1px as `[column, column + 1]` — so every marker in the layer, bullets and block icons alike, is half a pixel left of its own guide. Bullets and block icons also use different vertical anchors (a text rect's centre against roughly 5px above it). Both are resolved from one shared definition rather than per-consumer.
- **No new settings.** The demo's two dropdowns are removed; this is one behaviour.

## Spec impact

Two capabilities change, both deliberately:

- `outline-decorations` — **"a pure list renders byte-identical to outline-mode-off" is removed.** That invariant was chosen when the layer deferred all list geometry to Obsidian, and it is precisely what kept lists off the grid. The half that protects users is kept and restated: outline mode **off** renders exactly as stock Obsidian, for a pure list and for every other document. Nothing on disk changes either way — this was a rendering guarantee only.
- `hierarchy-position-indicators` — "Trail rendering through list nesting uses native list chrome or is omitted" is replaced. The omission existed because list levels had no column this plugin could address.

## What this PR contains

Planning and the reviewed demo. **The implementation follows.**

- `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` — the measurements, the prior art (obsidian-outliner, Minimal, the community threading snippets), the rejected alternatives, and the residuals.
- `openspec/changes/lists-on-the-outline-grid/` — proposal, two delta specs, design, tasks. `openspec validate --strict` passes.
- The demo build itself, behind `listLayout` and `listBullet` settings that default to today's rendering, plus `test-vault/Notes/List decoration demo.md` as the review fixture. Task group 4 removes both settings; the demo stays until then so the comparison remains available while implementing.

## Rejected alternatives, both built and measured

- **Measured overlays at native list columns** (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) — a second rendering mechanism with its own reflow bookkeeping, which Experiment 2b exists to avoid.
- **A DOM nudge to invalidate Obsidian's hang cache** — appending an empty hidden span to each list line and removing it works, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. Backed out: this repo's own lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a judgement, not a measurement. Stating the hang removes the need.

## Known residuals, recorded not fixed

- **Two- and three-space indented files.** Obsidian resolves only a tab or exactly four spaces into an indent unit, so those files are misaligned with the plugin disabled too — and our even guides make the mismatch more visible, not less. The durable fix is a normalize-indentation command, which is a structural-operations change.
- **Space-indented files depend on the user's "Show indentation guides" setting**, which controls whether the spans carrying list layout exist at all. Tab-indented files are unaffected.
- **Task checkboxes and wide ordered markers keep native geometry.** A checkbox lives in the marker span, is wider than the gutter, and is a real click target; right-aligning ordered numbers into the gutter needs a wrapper the DOM does not provide.
- **The indent unit does not become a user setting here** — it becomes a single declared value, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider layer-configurability item.

## Verification

Unit tests, lint, typecheck and the full desktop e2e suite are green on this branch. The change's own gate is task group 6: geometry assertions across tab / four-space / two-space, ordered, task and wrapping fixtures; the full corpus screenshotted in both bundled themes; a manual pass with Minimal installed (it sets `--list-indent` itself and puts its own margin on list lines); and a real-vault pass by hand — which is where every bug in this layer's history was actually found.

Proposal written and PR open: **[#54 — Put list decoration on the outline grid](https://github.com/laughedelic/obsidian-true-outliner/pull/54)** on `feat/lists-on-the-outline-grid`.

## On the bullet misalignment

Not a demo artifact — both are real and systematic, and I measured them so the implementation has numbers:

- **Horizontally**, every marker's centre sits at exactly `depth × unit`, but a guide paints its 1px as `[column, column + 1]`, so its visible centre is `column + 0.5`. Every marker in the layer is half a pixel left of its own guide — **block icons included**, unnoticed until a 4.8px dot next to a 1px line made it visible.
- **Vertically**, bullets and block icons don't share a rule at all. Measured against each line's own text rect: bullet `+0.00` (dead centre), paragraph icon `−5.20`, H1 icon `−8.45`. So the bullet is the one following the text and the block icons are the outliers — the opposite of what the report suggested, worth saying. The bullet still reads slightly high on its own, because a text rect spans ascender to descender while lowercase text's optical centre sits ~1.5px below its geometric middle.

Both are **task group 1** of the change, ahead of any list work: one shared column definition — horizontal and vertical — that the guide gradient, the marker offset and the accent layers all derive from, instead of three call sites agreeing by convention. It also folds in the pre-existing "vertical-alignment polish" entry for the widget-atom icons, since that's the same missing decision.

## Sub-decisions I made

You said go ahead, so I settled the three rather than blocking; all are in design.md with rationale and are cheap to revisit:

- **Task checkboxes keep native geometry** — the checkbox lives in the marker span, is wider than the gutter, and is a real click target I'd rather not reshape in passing.
- **Ordered markers start on the column** (`min-width`, not `width`, so `10. ` pushes its own text out instead of overlapping). Right-aligning into the gutter reads better but needs a wrapper the DOM doesn't provide.
- **The unit does not become a user setting here** — it becomes a single declared value, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider layer-configurability item.

## Contents

- `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` — measurements, prior art, both rejected alternatives, residuals.
- `openspec/changes/lists-on-the-outline-grid/` — proposal, two delta specs (`outline-decorations`, `hierarchy-position-indicators`), design, 6 task groups. `openspec validate --strict` passes.
- The demo build, still behind its settings so you can keep comparing; task group 4 removes them.

The PR body describes the intended change rather than the proposal process, and calls out the spec amendment prominently — removing "a pure list renders byte-identical to outline-mode-off" is the one thing a reviewer should push back on if they're going to.

Three commits, tree clean, unit/lint/typecheck green (e2e was green on the last full run before the artifacts landed; nothing since touches `src/`). Ready for `/opsx:apply` when you are.

9	Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:
10	
11	1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
12	   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on

16	   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
17	   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
18	   quantum that is not the Tab size.

20	   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
21	   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
22	4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
23	   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
24	   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
25	   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
26	   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.

31

43	- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
44	  three-space indentation). See Risks.

Design D7 now specifies picking the known keys instead of spreading, and task 4.3 became an implementation step with its own test rather than a confirmation that would have failed. This is the first setting the plugin has ever removed, so the allow-list is the general fix rather than a two-key patch.

**The spec was unmeetable as written.** "Markers and guides share one column definition" claimed every marker's visible centre coincides with its guide's — which design D5 deliberately doesn't deliver, since an ordered number can be wider than the marker gutter and a task checkbox is a control with its own hit area. Centring is now scoped to markers whose width this layer sets; the other two get an explicit weaker rule (start on the column, never left of it, never overlapping their own text) with a scenario each. content.text:
Both addressed and pushed as `b820499`; thread resolved, none left open.

**The task-line rule** — Copilot's reasoning was right but its prediction wasn't. Measured, a checkbox does *not* move between the two settings (55.33px at both), because Obsidian doesn't render a task marker inside the `.cm-formatting-list` span that `--list-padding-inline-start` reaches. So the unscoped rule was harmless — but it was harmless *by accident*, resting on a detail of how Obsidian renders a checkbox, while the two rules beside it stated the exclusion explicitly. All three now carry `:not(.HyperMD-task-line)`.

**Measuring it caught something bigger**, which the review didn't raise: my *previous* round's spec fix introduced a contradiction. The requirement says a checkbox SHALL start at its own depth column; design D5 said task lines "keep native geometry" outright. Measured, a checkbox starts **7.33px right of its column** while the bullets beside it are centred on it — the same off-the-grid mismatch this whole change exists to remove, just at smaller amplitude. D5 now excludes tasks from *centring* only, and a new task 3.5 brings the checkbox's start onto the column with its hit area verified by clicking rather than measuring, with an explicit escape hatch: if that's unsafe, amend the requirement deliberately with the measurement, don't leave spec and design disagreeing.

**The suppressed styles.css:93 comment** had no thread to reply to, but it was the most wrong thing in the diff, so I fixed it anyway. It claimed `--list-indent` carries Obsidian's hanging indent with it "so a soft-wrapped row still lands on the item's content column". That was true of my first probe and false of everything measured afterwards — the hang is a cached measurement whose invalidation ignores attribute changes, and it takes the end of the marker's *text* rather than its padded box. It was a stale claim from an early session sitting three directories away from the design doc that contradicts it.

754 unit tests, lint, typecheck and `openspec validate --strict` green; vault build refreshed so the demo still matches. [#54](https://github.com/laughedelic/obsidian-true-outliner/pull/54) is ready for `/opsx:apply`.

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1 && git push 2>&1 | tail -1
fix(decorations): resolve a line's guide depths once, and gate the bullet column

Three review findings plus a fixture regression the review work surfaced.

`activeGuideDepths` ran twice on every decorated line — once inside
`hasOverlay` and again to build the background — and twice more on the
widget-patched path. Each line now resolves it once and passes it down, and
`hasOverlay` takes the depths rather than recomputing them, with the bare
`trail !== undefined` test first. The sort inside it stays: the two tracks
genuinely interleave (a heading owning a list item owning a paragraph owning a
list gives [0, 2] and [1, 3]), and `LineGuideFact` documents both as ascending,
so concatenating would quietly break a property callers are told they have.
Nothing in the rendering depends on the order — the duplicate call was the
actual cost, not the comparison.

`to-list-bullet-column` was emitted whenever the bullet setting said so, even
with the layout still `native`. That combination pulls a bullet onto
`depth × unit` while the list is still stepping at Obsidian's own
`--list-indent`, putting it on a column nothing else in the document uses. The
class is now gated on the grid existing, and both settings say so where they
are declared.

`ListLayout`'s doc for `'grid'` still claimed wrapped rows "follow for free"
because Obsidian recomputes its hanging indent. Measured false, and already
corrected in styles.css two commits ago — the two now agree.

Also restores `test-vault/.obsidian/plugins/true-outliner/data.json` to its
baseline. A broad `git add -A` swept probe-run drift into the demo commit, so
the committed fixture carried `listLayout: own-guides` and `listBullet: column`
plus a stray outline path. That is the exact failure `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs`
was written for, named in its own doc comment, and it silently changed what four
position-indicator and selection-chrome assertions were measuring. The fixture is
back to defaults, keeping only the demo note it deliberately gained; the full
suite is green against it.
MSG

input.title: Fix npm run test:e2e in git worktrees
input.tldr: The e2e runner script looks for the wdio binary at a path that only exists in the main checkout, so the whole suite silently fails to start when run from a git worktree.
input.prompt:
In obsidian-true-outliner, `npm run test:e2e` fails immediately when run from a git worktree (e.g. `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`), with exit code 1 and no WebdriverIO output at all — it prints only the build and vault-drift lines, so it looks like the suite ran and produced nothing.

Cause: `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` has

    const bin = (name) => path.join(root, 'node_modules', '.bin', process.platform === 'win32' ? `${name}.cmd` : name);

and invokes `spawnSync(bin('wdio'), ...)`. A git worktree has no `node_modules/.bin` of its own — dependencies resolve up the directory chain to the main checkout — so that absolute path does not exist and `spawnSync` returns ENOENT with `status: null`, which `run(...)` coerces to 1. `npx wdio run e2e/wdio.conf.mts` works fine from the same worktree, as do vitest, tsc and eslint (they all resolve upward).

Fix suggestion: resolve the binary rather than assuming its location — e.g. try `bin(name)` and fall back to walking up parent directories for `node_modules/.bin/<name>`, or resolve `@wdio/cli`'s bin via `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@wdio/cli/bin/wdio.js')` and spawn it with `process.execPath`. Also worth making the ENOENT case loud instead of a bare exit code, since a silent "no output, exit 1" is what made this hard to diagnose.

Note that `scripts/run-e2e.mjs` was recently modified on main (spec groups / `e2e/wdio.shared.mts`), so check the current version before editing. Verify by running `npm run test:e2e` from both a worktree and the main checkout.

content.text:
All three addressed, rebased, and pushed as `149d9c5`. Threads replied to and resolved; none open.

**Two I fixed as asked.** The bullet-column class is now gated on the grid existing — that combination put the bullet on `depth × unit` while the list still stepped at Obsidian's own `--list-indent`, i.e. on a column nothing else in the document used. And the `'grid'` doc no longer claims wrapped rows "follow for free"; it now matches the `styles.css` comment I corrected last round.

**One I fixed differently than suggested.** The duplicate work was real — `activeGuideDepths` ran twice per plain line and twice more on the widget path — so each line now resolves it once and passes it down, with `hasOverlay` taking the depths and testing `trail !== undefined` first. But I kept the sort: the two tracks genuinely interleave. A heading owning a list item owning a paragraph owning a list gives `guideDepths [0, 2]` and `listGuideDepths [1, 3]`, and `LineGuideFact` documents both as ascending — concatenating would quietly break a property callers are told they have. The diagnosis was right about the waste and wrong about its cause.

## Two things this turn surfaced that the review didn't

**I committed test-vault drift.** The first full e2e run came back with four failures in the position-indicator and selection-chrome specs. They weren't the refactor — a broad `git add -A` in an earlier commit had swept probe-run drift into the committed fixture, so `data.json` carried `listLayout: own-guides` and `listBullet: column` plus a stray outline path, silently changing what those assertions measured. That is precisely the failure `scripts/check-vault-drift.mjs` exists to prevent and names in its own doc comment. Fixture restored to defaults, keeping only the demo note it deliberately gained.

**`main` moved under the branch.** The remote had been rebased onto a `main` that now carries `selection-aware-structural-ops` and new CI/e2e infrastructure. My three commits were intact there, so I replayed my one new commit onto it rather than force-pushing over the rebase. Re-verified on the new base: **818 unit tests, 21/21 e2e spec files**, lint, typecheck and `openspec validate --strict` all green, vault clean.

I also flagged a separate papercut as a background task: `npm run test:e2e` fails silently in a git worktree, because the runner builds an absolute `node_modules/.bin/wdio` path that only exists in the main checkout. Out of scope here, and it cost me a confusing dead end.

1	## Context
2	
3	See proposal.md for motivation, and
4	[docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md)
5	for the measurements every decision below rests on — taken live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the
6	e2e harness, then reviewed by hand in a demo build whose two experimental settings this change
7	removes.
8	
9	Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:
10	
11	1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
12	   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on
13	   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
14	   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.
15	2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
16	   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
17	   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
18	   quantum that is not the Tab size.
19	3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
20	   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
21	   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
22	4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
23	   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
24	   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
25	   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
26	   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.
27	
28	## Goals / Non-Goals
29	
30	**Goals:**
31	
32	- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
33	- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
34	  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
35	- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
36	  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
37	  one of ours.
38	
39	**Non-Goals:**
40	
41	- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
42	  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
43	- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
44	  three-space indentation). See Risks.
45	- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
46	  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
47	  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.
48	
49	## Decisions
50	
51	### D1 — Set the variables Obsidian reads, rather than positioning list lines ourselves
52	
53	Scope `--list-indent` (and the guide and marker-gap variables) to `.cm-line.to-decor-list`, the
54	class the decoration already puts on list-item lines. Both gates — outline mode, and lists only
55	— then come from the decoration itself and the CSS needs no second condition. Confirmed live:
56	an outline-mode note retargets and a non-outline note open beside it is byte-identical to
57	stock.
58	
59	*Alternatives considered.* Measuring each item's bullet and drawing overlays at those
60	coordinates (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) was the approach two earlier
61	probes concluded was the only one available. It is a second rendering mechanism with its own
62	reflow bookkeeping, and Experiment 2b replaced exactly that with the measurement-free gradient
63	the layer now rests on. Forcing a width onto `.cm-hmd-list-indent` per line was also built and
64	measured: the geometry is right and the caret round-trips, but it desynchronises Obsidian's
65	hanging indent (see D3) and needs a per-line custom property where a single variable does.
66	
67	### D2 — Draw the list guides ourselves; do not share with Obsidian's
68	
69	Suppress the native indent guide on our list lines (its width, not the user's setting, so the
70	`.cm-indent` spans that carry layout still exist) and lift `computeLineGuides`' list-item
71	exclusion so the existing gradient draws every level.
72	
73	Keeping the native guide was the cheaper option and was rejected on two measured grounds. It
74	disappears entirely when the user turns "Show indentation guides" off, so list levels would
75	lose their guides for a reason unrelated to outline mode. And it accents only ONE level — the
76	caret's own, via `.cm-active-indent` — where the trail accents the whole ancestor chain, so the
77	position indicator would still be missing inside lists, which is one of the things this change
78	exists to fix.
79	
80	`LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths in a field of their own rather than
81	merged into `guideDepths`. The walk publishes them unconditionally and the consumer combines
82	them, which keeps the fact independent of any rendering decision and keeps the per-`Text`
83	fact cache correct without a second key.
84	
85	### D3 — State the hanging indent; do not read Obsidian's
86	
87	Write `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent` on our list lines from
88	`(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter`, with `!important` — the rule this codebase
89	already relies on for `to-decor-block`, where an important stylesheet declaration beats
90	Obsidian's non-important inline style.
91	
92	Two measured defects close together. Obsidian derives the hang from `coordsAtPos` at the end of
93	the marker, which reports the end of the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box:
94	with the marker span sized to the gutter, every soft-wrapped list row lands 16px left of its
95	own item's text (measured 100.0 against a text column of 116.0). And because the value is
96	cached against attributes the observer does not watch, retargeting the grid at runtime — which
97	is what turning outline mode on does — leaves the old value in place until the note is
98	reopened. A stated value has neither problem: measured exact in both the freshly-opened and
99	the toggled-on case.
100	
101	*Alternative considered and rejected.* Provoking the `childList` mutation Obsidian's cache does
102	watch (append an empty hidden span to each list line, remove it again) was built and confirmed
103	to work, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. It was backed out: this repo's own
104	lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU
105	mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a
106	judgement rather than a measurement. Stating the value removes the need entirely.
107	
108	### D4 — The bullet is Obsidian's, positioned and weighted by us
109	
110	Keep the native `.list-bullet` rather than replacing it with a synthetic marker. It is already
111	a real element on the real column, it already carries the collapsed/hover states and the
112	accent hooks `hierarchy-position-indicators` uses, and its appearance is entirely
113	variable-driven (`--list-bullet-size`, `-radius`, `-border`, `-transform`,
114	`--list-marker-color`) — so customisable bullets later are a settings surface over variables,
115	not new geometry.
116	
117	Position: zero `--list-padding-inline-start`, a zero-width bullet box so its absolutely
118	positioned dot centres on the box's own start edge, and the whole marker span sized to the
119	marker gutter with `min-width`. Sizing the SPAN rather than padding the glyph is what makes the
120	text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction rather than the sum of a
121	padding, a glyph and a space.
122	
123	Weight: `--list-bullet-size: 0.38em`, colour token unchanged. Screenshotted at 0.30 (Obsidian's
124	default, 4.8px), 0.38, 0.45em and at `--text-muted`; 0.38em at the shared `--text-faint` lands

1	## ADDED Requirements
2	
3	### Requirement: One indentation grid for every kind
4	
5	In outline mode, the distance between one tree level and the next SHALL be the same for every
6	kind, including list items. A list level SHALL step by the outline unit rather than by
7	Obsidian's own list-indent value, so that a node's rendered column is a function of its tree
8	depth alone and never of the kind that encodes it.
9	
10	This SUPERSEDES the previous guarantee that a pure list renders byte-identical to
11	outline-mode-off. Byte-identity with stock Obsidian is now stated of outline mode OFF only:
12	with the mode off, every list — pure or not — SHALL render exactly as stock Obsidian renders
13	it, with no contribution from any decoration layer.
14	
15	The grid SHALL be derived from a single unit value used by every layer that positions
16	anything: indentation, guides, markers, and any accent drawn on them. A layer SHALL NOT
17	compute a column from a second source.
18	
19	Whether the SOURCE indentation of a list actually renders one unit per level is Obsidian's
20	own affair and is not guaranteed here: Obsidian resolves a tab or exactly four spaces into one
21	indent unit and renders anything shorter at its literal width. A document indented in units
22	Obsidian does not resolve renders its list levels at columns this requirement does not
23	control, with the mode on or off.
24	
25	#### Scenario: A list level and a heading level are the same distance
26	
27	- **WHEN** a document contains a heading three tree levels deep and a list item three tree
28	  levels deep, in a file indented with tabs
29	- **THEN** both render at the same column, and each level of the list is one unit from the
30	  last — the same unit that separates the heading levels
31	
32	#### Scenario: Ordered lists and task lists take the same grid
33	
34	- **WHEN** a nested ordered list and a nested task list are open in outline mode
35	- **THEN** each of their levels steps by the same unit as a bullet list's
36	
37	#### Scenario: Outline mode off is stock
38	
39	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned off on a note containing a nested list
40	- **THEN** every list line renders exactly as stock Obsidian renders it — the same columns,
41	  the same bullet, the same guides — with no decoration contribution of any kind
42	
43	#### Scenario: A note open without outline mode is unaffected by one that has it
44	
45	- **WHEN** one note with outline mode on and one without are open at the same time
46	- **THEN** the note without it renders its lists exactly as stock Obsidian does
47	
48	### Requirement: Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid
49	Every node's lines SHALL carry an indentation contribution equal to `depth × unit`,
50	computed from the node's distance from the document root in the parsed tree — not from raw
51	markdown indentation or heading level. Which CSS property carries that contribution SHALL be
52	determined by the line's RENDERED FORM, not by its node's kind: a line rendered as plain
53	text with no visible box of its own takes it as `padding-left`; a line that renders a
54	visible box of its own — an atom, or any line Obsidian replaces with an opaque widget —
55	takes it as `margin-left`, since padding does not move a visible box's own edges.
56	
57	A LIST ITEM takes its contribution in two parts, which together put it on that same grid:
58	`supplementalDepth × unit` as `margin-left`, where `supplementalDepth` is the count of
59	non-list-item ancestors above the nearest list root, plus the item's own depth WITHIN its
60	list, which Obsidian's own list rendering supplies once the outline unit is the unit it
61	renders a list level at. The plugin SHALL retarget that native rendering by supplying the
62	unit, and SHALL state the item's own hanging indent; it SHALL NOT reposition a list item by
63	overriding native rendering line by line.
64	
65	Nodes at the same tree depth SHALL receive the same indentation contribution regardless of
66	whether their depth is encoded via heading level, list indentation, or paragraph adjacency,
67	AND regardless of whether the line is currently rendered as plain text or as an opaque widget.
68	
69	#### Scenario: Heading and list depth align
70	- **WHEN** a `### Heading` two tree-levels deep (nested under an `#` and a `##` ancestor)
71	  and a twice-indented list item are both visible in the same document
72	- **THEN** both render the same indentation contribution
73	
74	#### Scenario: A list shifts as a whole under a non-list ancestor, and steps by the unit within itself
75	- **WHEN** a list sits under a heading
76	- **THEN** the list's start position shifts right by the heading's own depth contribution,
77	  and each of its own nesting levels is one unit from the last — the same unit the heading
78	  levels use
79	
80	#### Scenario: Multiline continuation lines match their node's first line
81	- **WHEN** a paragraph or list item spans multiple physical lines (via a hard line break)
82	- **THEN** every continuation line carries the same indentation contribution as the node's
83	  first line
84	
85	#### Scenario: A widget-rendered line aligns with its same-depth plain siblings
86	- **WHEN** a line whose node is NOT an atom (e.g. a paragraph consisting of a note embed,
87	  `![[Another note]]`) is rendered by Obsidian as an opaque replacement element, and a plain
88	  paragraph sits at the same tree depth in the same document
89	- **THEN** both start at the same column — the widget-rendered line's indentation
90	  contribution is its node's, exactly as though it had rendered as plain text
91	
92	### Requirement: A list item's hanging indent is stated, not measured
93	
94	A list item's soft-wrapped rows SHALL align with the start of that item's own content. The
95	plugin SHALL state that alignment from the values it already knows — the item's tree depth,
96	its list root's depth, the unit, and the marker gutter — rather than relying on a measurement
97	of the rendered marker.
98	
99	This is required because a measurement of the marker's own extent reports where its TEXT ends
100	rather than where the item's content begins, and because a measurement is cached against the
101	rendering that produced it and does not follow a later change to the grid.
102	
103	#### Scenario: A wrapped nested item aligns under its own text
104	
105	- **WHEN** a list item several levels deep is long enough to soft-wrap
106	- **THEN** its wrapped rows start at the same column as its own first row's text, not at the
107	  marker column and not at the line start
108	
109	#### Scenario: Turning outline mode on corrects wrapping immediately
110	
111	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned on for a note already open, containing a soft-wrapping
112	  nested list item
113	- **THEN** that item's wrapped rows align with its content on the same render, with no note
114	  switch, reload, or edit required
115

117	
118	Every layer that positions something at a depth's column — the guide gradient, a marker's own

120	two of them can be changed independently.

123	visible centre of a guide line and the visible centre of the marker on it coincide. That is
124	every synthetic block marker and an unordered list item's native bullet.
125	
126	Two native markers are explicitly EXCLUDED from the centring rule, because their width is not
127	this layer's to set: an ordered item's number, which can be wider than the marker gutter, and
128	a task item's checkbox, which is a control with its own hit area. Each SHALL instead START at
129	its own depth column, and SHALL NOT render left of it or overlap the item's own text.
130	
131	A marker's VERTICAL placement SHALL follow one rule across kinds — including the two excluded
132	above: a marker SHALL sit at the same position relative to its own node's first text row
133	whatever the node's kind, so markers on adjacent rows read as one column.

**The decorate.ts finding was a real bug in code I wrote.** `computeLineGuides` reset `listGuideDepths` to empty at every non-list node, and my own comment justified it: a non-list node "ends the list chain". Without that negative control I'd have shipped a test that couldn't fail and reported the bug as pinned.

15	2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
16	   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
17	   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
18	   quantum that is not the Tab size.
19	3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
20	   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
21	   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
22	4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
23	   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
24	   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
25	   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
26	   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.
27	
28	## Goals / Non-Goals
29	
30	**Goals:**
31	
32	- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
33	- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
34	  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
35	- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
36	  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
37	  one of ours.
38	
39	**Non-Goals:**
40	
41	- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
42	  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
43	- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
44	  three-space indentation). See Risks.
45	- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
46	  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
47	  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.
48	
49	## Decisions
50	
51	### D1 — Set the variables Obsidian reads, rather than positioning list lines ourselves
52	
53	Scope `--list-indent` (and the guide and marker-gap variables) to `.cm-line.to-decor-list`, the
54	class the decoration already puts on list-item lines. Both gates — outline mode, and lists only
55	— then come from the decoration itself and the CSS needs no second condition. Confirmed live:
56	an outline-mode note retargets and a non-outline note open beside it is byte-identical to
57	stock.
58	
59	*Alternatives considered.* Measuring each item's bullet and drawing overlays at those
60	coordinates (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) was the approach two earlier
61	probes concluded was the only one available. It is a second rendering mechanism with its own
62	reflow bookkeeping, and Experiment 2b replaced exactly that with the measurement-free gradient
63	the layer now rests on. Forcing a width onto `.cm-hmd-list-indent` per line was also built and
64	measured: the geometry is right and the caret round-trips, but it desynchronises Obsidian's
65	hanging indent (see D3) and needs a per-line custom property where a single variable does.
66	
67	### D2 — Draw the list guides ourselves; do not share with Obsidian's
68	
69	Suppress the native indent guide on our list lines (its width, not the user's setting, so the
70	`.cm-indent` spans that carry layout still exist) and lift `computeLineGuides`' list-item
71	exclusion so the existing gradient draws every level.
72	
73	Keeping the native guide was the cheaper option and was rejected on two measured grounds. It
74	disappears entirely when the user turns "Show indentation guides" off, so list levels would
75	lose their guides for a reason unrelated to outline mode. And it accents only ONE level — the
76	caret's own, via `.cm-active-indent` — where the trail accents the whole ancestor chain, so the
77	position indicator would still be missing inside lists, which is one of the things this change
78	exists to fix.
79	
80	`LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths in a field of their own rather than
81	merged into `guideDepths`. The walk publishes them unconditionally and the consumer combines
82	them, which keeps the fact independent of any rendering decision and keeps the per-`Text`
83	fact cache correct without a second key.
84	
85	### D3 — State the hanging indent; do not read Obsidian's
86	
87	Write `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent` on our list lines from
88	`(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter`, with `!important` — the rule this codebase
89	already relies on for `to-decor-block`, where an important stylesheet declaration beats
90	Obsidian's non-important inline style.
91	
92	Two measured defects close together. Obsidian derives the hang from `coordsAtPos` at the end of
93	the marker, which reports the end of the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box:
94	with the marker span sized to the gutter, every soft-wrapped list row lands 16px left of its
95	own item's text (measured 100.0 against a text column of 116.0). And because the value is
96	cached against attributes the observer does not watch, retargeting the grid at runtime — which
97	is what turning outline mode on does — leaves the old value in place until the note is
98	reopened. A stated value has neither problem: measured exact in both the freshly-opened and
99	the toggled-on case.
100	
101	*Alternative considered and rejected.* Provoking the `childList` mutation Obsidian's cache does
102	watch (append an empty hidden span to each list line, remove it again) was built and confirmed
103	to work, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. It was backed out: this repo's own
104	lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU
105	mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a
106	judgement rather than a measurement. Stating the value removes the need entirely.
107	
108	### D4 — The bullet is Obsidian's, positioned and weighted by us
109	
110	Keep the native `.list-bullet` rather than replacing it with a synthetic marker. It is already
111	a real element on the real column, it already carries the collapsed/hover states and the
112	accent hooks `hierarchy-position-indicators` uses, and its appearance is entirely
113	variable-driven (`--list-bullet-size`, `-radius`, `-border`, `-transform`,
114	`--list-marker-color`) — so customisable bullets later are a settings surface over variables,
115	not new geometry.
116	
117	Position: zero `--list-padding-inline-start`, a zero-width bullet box so its absolutely
118	positioned dot centres on the box's own start edge, and the whole marker span sized to the
119	marker gutter with `min-width`. Sizing the SPAN rather than padding the glyph is what makes the
120	text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction rather than the sum of a
121	padding, a glyph and a space.
122	
123	Weight: `--list-bullet-size: 0.38em`, colour token unchanged. Screenshotted at 0.30 (Obsidian's
124	default, 4.8px), 0.38, 0.45em and at `--text-muted`; 0.38em at the shared `--text-faint` lands

1	## ADDED Requirements
2	
3	### Requirement: One indentation grid for every kind
4	
5	In outline mode, the distance between one tree level and the next SHALL be the same for every
6	kind, including list items. A list level SHALL step by the outline unit rather than by
7	Obsidian's own list-indent value, so that a node's rendered column is a function of its tree
8	depth alone and never of the kind that encodes it.
9	
10	This SUPERSEDES the previous guarantee that a pure list renders byte-identical to
11	outline-mode-off. Byte-identity with stock Obsidian is now stated of outline mode OFF only:
12	with the mode off, every list — pure or not — SHALL render exactly as stock Obsidian renders
13	it, with no contribution from any decoration layer.
14	
15	The grid SHALL be derived from a single unit value used by every layer that positions
16	anything: indentation, guides, markers, and any accent drawn on them. A layer SHALL NOT
17	compute a column from a second source.
18	
19	Whether the SOURCE indentation of a list actually renders one unit per level is Obsidian's
20	own affair and is not guaranteed here: Obsidian resolves a tab or exactly four spaces into one
21	indent unit and renders anything shorter at its literal width. A document indented in units
22	Obsidian does not resolve renders its list levels at columns this requirement does not
23	control, with the mode on or off.
24	
25	#### Scenario: A list level and a heading level are the same distance
26	
27	- **WHEN** a document contains a heading three tree levels deep and a list item three tree
28	  levels deep, in a file indented with tabs
29	- **THEN** both render at the same column, and each level of the list is one unit from the
30	  last — the same unit that separates the heading levels
31	
32	#### Scenario: Ordered lists and task lists take the same grid
33	
34	- **WHEN** a nested ordered list and a nested task list are open in outline mode
35	- **THEN** each of their levels steps by the same unit as a bullet list's
36	
37	#### Scenario: Outline mode off is stock
38	
39	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned off on a note containing a nested list
40	- **THEN** every list line renders exactly as stock Obsidian renders it — the same columns,
41	  the same bullet, the same guides — with no decoration contribution of any kind
42	
43	#### Scenario: A note open without outline mode is unaffected by one that has it
44	
45	- **WHEN** one note with outline mode on and one without are open at the same time
46	- **THEN** the note without it renders its lists exactly as stock Obsidian does
47	
48	### Requirement: Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid
49	Every node's lines SHALL carry an indentation contribution equal to `depth × unit`,
50	computed from the node's distance from the document root in the parsed tree — not from raw
51	markdown indentation or heading level. Which CSS property carries that contribution SHALL be
52	determined by the line's RENDERED FORM, not by its node's kind: a line rendered as plain
53	text with no visible box of its own takes it as `padding-left`; a line that renders a
54	visible box of its own — an atom, or any line Obsidian replaces with an opaque widget —
55	takes it as `margin-left`, since padding does not move a visible box's own edges.
56	
57	A LIST ITEM takes its contribution in two parts, which together put it on that same grid:
58	`supplementalDepth × unit` as `margin-left`, where `supplementalDepth` is the count of
59	non-list-item ancestors above the nearest list root, plus the item's own depth WITHIN its
60	list, which Obsidian's own list rendering supplies once the outline unit is the unit it
61	renders a list level at. The plugin SHALL retarget that native rendering by supplying the
62	unit, and SHALL state the item's own hanging indent; it SHALL NOT reposition a list item by
63	overriding native rendering line by line.
64	
65	Nodes at the same tree depth SHALL receive the same indentation contribution regardless of
66	whether their depth is encoded via heading level, list indentation, or paragraph adjacency,
67	AND regardless of whether the line is currently rendered as plain text or as an opaque widget.
68	
69	#### Scenario: Heading and list depth align
70	- **WHEN** a `### Heading` two tree-levels deep (nested under an `#` and a `##` ancestor)
71	  and a twice-indented list item are both visible in the same document
72	- **THEN** both render the same indentation contribution
73	
74	#### Scenario: A list shifts as a whole under a non-list ancestor, and steps by the unit within itself
75	- **WHEN** a list sits under a heading
76	- **THEN** the list's start position shifts right by the heading's own depth contribution,
77	  and each of its own nesting levels is one unit from the last — the same unit the heading
78	  levels use
79	
80	#### Scenario: Multiline continuation lines match their node's first line
81	- **WHEN** a paragraph or list item spans multiple physical lines (via a hard line break)
82	- **THEN** every continuation line carries the same indentation contribution as the node's
83	  first line
84	
85	#### Scenario: A widget-rendered line aligns with its same-depth plain siblings
86	- **WHEN** a line whose node is NOT an atom (e.g. a paragraph consisting of a note embed,
87	  `![[Another note]]`) is rendered by Obsidian as an opaque replacement element, and a plain
88	  paragraph sits at the same tree depth in the same document
89	- **THEN** both start at the same column — the widget-rendered line's indentation
90	  contribution is its node's, exactly as though it had rendered as plain text
91	
92	### Requirement: A list item's hanging indent is stated, not measured
93	
94	A list item's soft-wrapped rows SHALL align with the start of that item's own content. The
95	plugin SHALL state that alignment from the values it already knows — the item's tree depth,
96	its list root's depth, the unit, and the marker gutter — rather than relying on a measurement
97	of the rendered marker.
98	
99	This is required because a measurement of the marker's own extent reports where its TEXT ends

102	
103	#### Scenario: A wrapped nested item aligns under its own text

107	  marker column and not at the line start

109	#### Scenario: Turning outline mode on corrects wrapping immediately
110	
111	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned on for a note already open, containing a soft-wrapping
112	  nested list item

fix(decorations): a list line publishes the marker gutter it is sized by

The experimental marker-column rule sizes a list item's marker span with
`min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter, 1.25rem)`, but list lines never set that
variable — only block and atom lines do, from `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS`. So the
gutter had two definitions: the TS constant every other kind uses, and a
literal in the CSS fallback that had to be kept equal to it by hand.

List lines now publish it too. No rendering change — `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` is
`1.25rem` and the fallback was `1.25rem`, and nothing else on a list line reads
the variable (its own margin calc does not include a gutter term, and
`plainOwnShiftExpr` returns before the atom branch that does). What changes is
that the two can no longer drift apart, which is the same one-number-one-source
rule task 1.1 states for the column itself. styles.css says why the variable is
set on a line that reserves no gutter of its own.
MSG

content.text:
Fixed and pushed as `edfa1ec`. No `comment_id` on that one, so there's no thread to reply to or resolve — and none are open.

**The finding was right.** The marker span was sized by `min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter, 1.25rem)`, but only block and atom lines published that variable; list lines relied on the fallback. So the gutter had two definitions — `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` in TS and a literal in the CSS — that had to be kept equal by hand. List lines now publish it too. It's a no-op today (both are `1.25rem`, and nothing else on a list line reads the variable), but it's the same one-number-one-source rule task 1.1 already states for the column.

## One thing to flag about verification

I could not re-run the full test suite cleanly. The machine is under heavy external load — load average ~16, NordVPN sitting at 106% CPU — and vitest got 7% of a core, stretching 71 seconds of work across 17 minutes. Under that, a different random subset of fast-check property tests times out each run: 3 failures, then 7, then 3, all in unrelated areas (group ops, covers, deletions), each reporting durations of 650–1000 *seconds* for tests that normally take milliseconds.

So, precisely what I did and didn't verify on this commit:

- **Verified**: typecheck, lint, and `tests/decorate.test.ts` (91/91 in 0.8s).
- **Verified by reading**: the change is value-identical — `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` is `1.25rem`, the fallback was `1.25rem`, and I grepped every consumer of the variable to confirm no list-line path reads it elsewhere. I'd also measured the span at 20px earlier.
- **Not re-run**: the full unit suite and the e2e suite. Both were green on the previous commit (`2b26cac`: 820 unit tests, 21/21 e2e).

I chose not to keep re-running under that load — it would add contention to a machine you're using and wouldn't produce a trustworthy result. Say the word when it's quiet and I'll do a clean full pass; CI will also cover it on the PR.

content.text:
Pushed as `761b541`. CI will verify on a clean runner.

## What broke and why

CI was right, and the cause was my previous commit. The test `leaves a pure list's geometry byte-identical to outline-mode-off` snapshots the **custom properties themselves**, so publishing `--to-marker-gutter` on every list line made a mode-on pure list differ from a mode-off one by `"" → "1.25rem"`. My "no rendering change" claim was true of rendering and false of the DOM — and the requirement it violated is one this change removes *later*. It's still in force now, so the guard fired correctly.

The fix: both variables the demo adds to a list line (`--to-depth` and `--to-marker-gutter`) are read only by the experimental list-grid rules, so they're now published only when those rules are on. At default settings a list line carries exactly what it did before the demo. I verified the fix against the assertion directly — `geometrySnapshot()` reads `--to-marker-gutter` per line, and with `listLayout: 'native'` the gate pushes nothing.

**This reached CI because I pushed that commit without an e2e run.** I was right that the local suite couldn't produce a trustworthy signal, and wrong to push anyway.

## Why I'm not verifying locally

This machine can't run the e2e suite usefully right now. Three runs of that one spec, same code:

| Run | Duration (normally ~35s) | Failures |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 26m 47s | widget-rendered ancestor; no-geometry-change; both-off baseline |
| 2 | 32m 25s | ancestor full extent; ancestor markers with guides off |

Zero overlap between the failure sets, and the test CI actually failed on **passed in both**. That's the signature of starvation, not a defect — a real one fails the same test every time. Sustained load average 5–8 with no single hog; I checked for orphaned chromedriver/wdio/Obsidian processes from my own backgrounded runs and there are none, so it's ambient load from your environment (Claude, Comet, WindowServer), not something I left behind.

So: `tsc`, `lint` and `tests/decorate.test.ts` are green locally, the fix is verified by reading the exact assertion, and CI on a clean runner is the arbiter for the rest. I'd rather say that than report a green I don't have. If you want a local full pass, tell me when the machine is quiet.
