1	## Context
2	
3	See proposal.md for motivation, and
4	[docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md)
5	for the measurements every decision below rests on — taken live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the
6	e2e harness, then reviewed by hand in a demo build whose two experimental settings this change
7	removes.
8	
9	Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:
10	
11	1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
12	   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on
13	   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
14	   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.
15	2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
16	   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
17	   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
18	   quantum that is not the Tab size.
19	3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
20	   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
21	   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
22	4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
23	   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
24	   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
25	   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
26	   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.
27	
28	## Goals / Non-Goals
29	
30	**Goals:**
31	
32	- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
33	- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
34	  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
35	- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
36	  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
37	  one of ours.
38	
39	**Non-Goals:**
40	
41	- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
42	  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
43	- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
44	  three-space indentation). See Risks.
45	- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
46	  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
47	  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.
48	
49	## Decisions
50	
51	### D1 — Set the variables Obsidian reads, rather than positioning list lines ourselves
52	
53	Scope `--list-indent` (and the guide and marker-gap variables) to `.cm-line.to-decor-list`, the
54	class the decoration already puts on list-item lines. Both gates — outline mode, and lists only
55	— then come from the decoration itself and the CSS needs no second condition. Confirmed live:
56	an outline-mode note retargets and a non-outline note open beside it is byte-identical to
57	stock.
58	
59	*Alternatives considered.* Measuring each item's bullet and drawing overlays at those
60	coordinates (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) was the approach two earlier
61	probes concluded was the only one available. It is a second rendering mechanism with its own
62	reflow bookkeeping, and Experiment 2b replaced exactly that with the measurement-free gradient
63	the layer now rests on. Forcing a width onto `.cm-hmd-list-indent` per line was also built and
64	measured: the geometry is right and the caret round-trips, but it desynchronises Obsidian's
65	hanging indent (see D3) and needs a per-line custom property where a single variable does.
66	
67	### D2 — Draw the list guides ourselves; do not share with Obsidian's
68	
69	Suppress the native indent guide on our list lines (its width, not the user's setting, so the
70	`.cm-indent` spans that carry layout still exist) and lift `computeLineGuides`' list-item
71	exclusion so the existing gradient draws every level.
72	
73	Keeping the native guide was the cheaper option and was rejected on two measured grounds. It
74	disappears entirely when the user turns "Show indentation guides" off, so list levels would
75	lose their guides for a reason unrelated to outline mode. And it accents only ONE level — the
76	caret's own, via `.cm-active-indent` — where the trail accents the whole ancestor chain, so the
77	position indicator would still be missing inside lists, which is one of the things this change
78	exists to fix.
79	
80	`LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths in a field of their own rather than
81	merged into `guideDepths`. The walk publishes them unconditionally and the consumer combines
82	them, which keeps the fact independent of any rendering decision and keeps the per-`Text`
83	fact cache correct without a second key.
84	
85	### D3 — State the hanging indent; do not read Obsidian's
86	
87	Write `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent` on our list lines from
88	`(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter`, with `!important` — the rule this codebase
89	already relies on for `to-decor-block`, where an important stylesheet declaration beats
90	Obsidian's non-important inline style.
91	
92	Two measured defects close together. Obsidian derives the hang from `coordsAtPos` at the end of
93	the marker, which reports the end of the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box:
94	with the marker span sized to the gutter, every soft-wrapped list row lands 16px left of its
95	own item's text (measured 100.0 against a text column of 116.0). And because the value is
96	cached against attributes the observer does not watch, retargeting the grid at runtime — which
97	is what turning outline mode on does — leaves the old value in place until the note is
98	reopened. A stated value has neither problem: measured exact in both the freshly-opened and
99	the toggled-on case.
100	
101	*Alternative considered and rejected.* Provoking the `childList` mutation Obsidian's cache does
102	watch (append an empty hidden span to each list line, remove it again) was built and confirmed
103	to work, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. It was backed out: this repo's own
104	lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU
105	mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a
106	judgement rather than a measurement. Stating the value removes the need entirely.
107	
108	### D4 — The bullet is Obsidian's, positioned and weighted by us
109	
110	Keep the native `.list-bullet` rather than replacing it with a synthetic marker. It is already
111	a real element on the real column, it already carries the collapsed/hover states and the
112	accent hooks `hierarchy-position-indicators` uses, and its appearance is entirely
113	variable-driven (`--list-bullet-size`, `-radius`, `-border`, `-transform`,
114	`--list-marker-color`) — so customisable bullets later are a settings surface over variables,
115	not new geometry.
116	
117	Position: zero `--list-padding-inline-start`, a zero-width bullet box so its absolutely
118	positioned dot centres on the box's own start edge, and the whole marker span sized to the
119	marker gutter with `min-width`. Sizing the SPAN rather than padding the glyph is what makes the
120	text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction rather than the sum of a
121	padding, a glyph and a space.
122	
123	Weight: `--list-bullet-size: 0.38em`, colour token unchanged. Screenshotted at 0.30 (Obsidian's
124	default, 4.8px), 0.38, 0.45em and at `--text-muted`; 0.38em at the shared `--text-faint` lands

1	## ADDED Requirements
2	
3	### Requirement: One indentation grid for every kind
4	
5	In outline mode, the distance between one tree level and the next SHALL be the same for every
6	kind, including list items. A list level SHALL step by the outline unit rather than by
7	Obsidian's own list-indent value, so that a node's rendered column is a function of its tree
8	depth alone and never of the kind that encodes it.
9	
10	This SUPERSEDES the previous guarantee that a pure list renders byte-identical to
11	outline-mode-off. Byte-identity with stock Obsidian is now stated of outline mode OFF only:
12	with the mode off, every list — pure or not — SHALL render exactly as stock Obsidian renders
13	it, with no contribution from any decoration layer.
14	
15	The grid SHALL be derived from a single unit value used by every layer that positions
16	anything: indentation, guides, markers, and any accent drawn on them. A layer SHALL NOT
17	compute a column from a second source.
18	
19	Whether the SOURCE indentation of a list actually renders one unit per level is Obsidian's
20	own affair and is not guaranteed here: Obsidian resolves a tab or exactly four spaces into one
21	indent unit and renders anything shorter at its literal width. A document indented in units
22	Obsidian does not resolve renders its list levels at columns this requirement does not
23	control, with the mode on or off.
24	
25	#### Scenario: A list level and a heading level are the same distance
26	
27	- **WHEN** a document contains a heading three tree levels deep and a list item three tree
28	  levels deep, in a file indented with tabs
29	- **THEN** both render at the same column, and each level of the list is one unit from the
30	  last — the same unit that separates the heading levels
31	
32	#### Scenario: Ordered lists and task lists take the same grid
33	
34	- **WHEN** a nested ordered list and a nested task list are open in outline mode
35	- **THEN** each of their levels steps by the same unit as a bullet list's
36	
37	#### Scenario: Outline mode off is stock
38	
39	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned off on a note containing a nested list
40	- **THEN** every list line renders exactly as stock Obsidian renders it — the same columns,
41	  the same bullet, the same guides — with no decoration contribution of any kind
42	
43	#### Scenario: A note open without outline mode is unaffected by one that has it
44	
45	- **WHEN** one note with outline mode on and one without are open at the same time
46	- **THEN** the note without it renders its lists exactly as stock Obsidian does
47	
48	### Requirement: Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid
49	Every node's lines SHALL carry an indentation contribution equal to `depth × unit`,
50	computed from the node's distance from the document root in the parsed tree — not from raw
51	markdown indentation or heading level. Which CSS property carries that contribution SHALL be
52	determined by the line's RENDERED FORM, not by its node's kind: a line rendered as plain
53	text with no visible box of its own takes it as `padding-left`; a line that renders a
54	visible box of its own — an atom, or any line Obsidian replaces with an opaque widget —
55	takes it as `margin-left`, since padding does not move a visible box's own edges.
56	
57	A LIST ITEM takes its contribution in two parts, which together put it on that same grid:
58	`supplementalDepth × unit` as `margin-left`, where `supplementalDepth` is the count of
59	non-list-item ancestors above the nearest list root, plus the item's own depth WITHIN its
60	list, which Obsidian's own list rendering supplies once the outline unit is the unit it
61	renders a list level at. The plugin SHALL retarget that native rendering by supplying the
62	unit, and SHALL state the item's own hanging indent; it SHALL NOT reposition a list item by
63	overriding native rendering line by line.
64	
65	Nodes at the same tree depth SHALL receive the same indentation contribution regardless of
66	whether their depth is encoded via heading level, list indentation, or paragraph adjacency,
67	AND regardless of whether the line is currently rendered as plain text or as an opaque widget.
68	
69	#### Scenario: Heading and list depth align
70	- **WHEN** a `### Heading` two tree-levels deep (nested under an `#` and a `##` ancestor)
71	  and a twice-indented list item are both visible in the same document
72	- **THEN** both render the same indentation contribution
73	
74	#### Scenario: A list shifts as a whole under a non-list ancestor, and steps by the unit within itself
75	- **WHEN** a list sits under a heading
76	- **THEN** the list's start position shifts right by the heading's own depth contribution,
77	  and each of its own nesting levels is one unit from the last — the same unit the heading
78	  levels use
79	
80	#### Scenario: Multiline continuation lines match their node's first line
81	- **WHEN** a paragraph or list item spans multiple physical lines (via a hard line break)
82	- **THEN** every continuation line carries the same indentation contribution as the node's
83	  first line
84	
85	#### Scenario: A widget-rendered line aligns with its same-depth plain siblings
86	- **WHEN** a line whose node is NOT an atom (e.g. a paragraph consisting of a note embed,
87	  `![[Another note]]`) is rendered by Obsidian as an opaque replacement element, and a plain
88	  paragraph sits at the same tree depth in the same document
89	- **THEN** both start at the same column — the widget-rendered line's indentation
90	  contribution is its node's, exactly as though it had rendered as plain text
91	
92	### Requirement: A list item's hanging indent is stated, not measured
93	
94	A list item's soft-wrapped rows SHALL align with the start of that item's own content. The
95	plugin SHALL state that alignment from the values it already knows — the item's tree depth,
96	its list root's depth, the unit, and the marker gutter — rather than relying on a measurement
97	of the rendered marker.
98	
99	This is required because a measurement of the marker's own extent reports where its TEXT ends
100	rather than where the item's content begins, and because a measurement is cached against the
101	rendering that produced it and does not follow a later change to the grid.
102	
103	#### Scenario: A wrapped nested item aligns under its own text
104	
105	- **WHEN** a list item several levels deep is long enough to soft-wrap
106	- **THEN** its wrapped rows start at the same column as its own first row's text, not at the
107	  marker column and not at the line start
108	
109	#### Scenario: Turning outline mode on corrects wrapping immediately
110	
111	- **WHEN** outline mode is turned on for a note already open, containing a soft-wrapping
112	  nested list item
113	- **THEN** that item's wrapped rows align with its content on the same render, with no note
114	  switch, reload, or edit required
115	
116	### Requirement: Markers and guides share one column definition
117	
118	Every layer that positions something at a depth's column — the guide gradient, a marker's own
119	offset, and any accent drawn on either — SHALL derive that column from ONE definition, so no
120	two of them can be changed independently.
121	
122	A marker whose width this layer controls SHALL have its visible centre on that column, so the
123	visible centre of a guide line and the visible centre of the marker on it coincide. That is
124	every synthetic block marker and an unordered list item's native bullet.
125	
126	Two native markers are explicitly EXCLUDED from the centring rule, because their width is not
127	this layer's to set: an ordered item's number, which can be wider than the marker gutter, and
128	a task item's checkbox, which is a control with its own hit area. Each SHALL instead START at
129	its own depth column, and SHALL NOT render left of it or overlap the item's own text.
130	
131	A marker's VERTICAL placement SHALL follow one rule across kinds — including the two excluded
132	above: a marker SHALL sit at the same position relative to its own node's first text row
133	whatever the node's kind, so markers on adjacent rows read as one column.
134

Base directory for this skill: /Users/laughedelic/Code/obsidian-true-outliner/.claude/worktrees/native-lists-decoration-5f72c7/.claude/skills/openspec-apply-change

Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change.

**Store selection:** If the user names a store (a store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on this machine) or the work lives in one, run `openspec store list --json` to discover registered store ids, then pass `--store <id>` on the commands that read or write specs and changes (`new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `list`, `show`, `validate`, `archive`, `doctor`, `context`, `view`). Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Input**: Optionally specify a change name (e.g., `/opsx:apply add-auth`). If omitted, check if it can be inferred from conversation context. If vague or ambiguous you MUST prompt for available changes.

**Steps**

1. **Select the change**

   If a name is provided, use it. Otherwise:
   - Infer from conversation context if the user mentioned a change
   - Auto-select if only one active change exists
   - If ambiguous, run `openspec list --json` to get available changes and ask the user to select one

   Always announce: "Using change: <name>" and how to override (e.g., `/opsx:apply <other>`).

2. **Check status to understand the schema**
   ```bash
   openspec status --change "<name>" --json
   ```
   Parse the JSON to understand:
   - `schemaName`: The workflow being used (e.g., "spec-driven")
   - `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, and `actionContext`: planning scope and edit constraints
   - Which artifact contains the tasks (typically "tasks" for spec-driven, check status for others)

3. **Get apply instructions**

   ```bash
   openspec instructions apply --change "<name>" --json
   ```

   This returns:
   - `contextFiles`: artifact ID -> array of concrete file paths (varies by schema - could be proposal/specs/design/tasks or spec/tests/implementation/docs)
   - Progress (total, complete, remaining)
   - Task list with status
   - Dynamic instruction based on current state
   - Optional `context`: current required project instruction input from the selected root
   - Optional `operationGuidance`: current advisory guidance for apply

   **Handle states:**
   - If `state: "blocked"` (missing artifacts): show message, suggest using `/opsx:continue` (if it is not installed, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json` to see the next artifact and `openspec instructions <artifact-id> --change "<name>" --json` for how to create it)
   - If `state: "all_done"`: congratulate, suggest archive
   - Otherwise: proceed to implementation

   Treat `context` as a required prompt-level input. Read and consider it, and
   apply relevant project facts, conventions, and constraints while implementing.
   Treat `operationGuidance` as optional additive advice. Read and consider every
   entry, and follow entries that are applicable and compatible with the built-in
   workflow.

   Keep both fields separate from CLI-returned state, missing artifacts, tasks,
   progress, `contextFiles`, and the built-in `instruction`. They are not
   evidence of task completion, do not replace the built-in instruction, and do
   not permit bypassing a blocked state. If context conflicts with the built-in
   instruction, an explicit user choice, or a CLI-controlled value, report the
   conflict and preserve the controlling value. If guidance is inapplicable or
   conflicts with those controlling inputs, do not follow it and explain why.
   These are prompt-level behavior contracts, not enforceable checks.

4. **Read context files**

   Read every file path listed under `contextFiles` from the apply instructions output.
   The files depend on the schema being used:
   - **spec-driven**: proposal, specs, design, tasks
   - Other schemas: follow the contextFiles from CLI output

   Do not copy `context` or `operationGuidance` verbatim into implementation
   files or planning artifacts unless the user separately asks for that content.

5. **Show current progress**

   Display:
   - Schema being used
   - Progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - Remaining tasks overview
   - Dynamic instruction from CLI

6. **Implement tasks (loop until done or blocked)**

   For each pending task:
   - Show which task is being worked on
   - Make the code changes required
   - Keep changes minimal and focused
   - Mark task complete in the tasks file: `- [ ]` → `- [x]`
   - Continue to next task

   **Pause if:**
   - Task is unclear → ask for clarification
   - Implementation reveals a design issue → suggest updating artifacts
   - Error or blocker encountered → report and wait for guidance
   - User interrupts

7. **On completion or pause, show status**

   Display:
   - Tasks completed this session
   - Overall progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - If all done: suggest archive
   - If paused: explain why and wait for guidance

**Output During Implementation**

```
## Implementing: <change-name> (schema: <schema-name>)

Working on task 3/7: <task description>
[...implementation happening...]
✓ Task complete

Working on task 4/7: <task description>

**Output On Pause (Issue Encountered)**

**Progress:** 4/7 tasks complete

### Issue Encountered
<description of the issue>

**Options:**

What would you like to do?
```

**Guardrails**
- Keep going through tasks until done or blocked
- Always read context files before starting (from the apply instructions output)
- If task is ambiguous, pause and ask before implementing
- If implementation reveals issues, pause and suggest artifact updates
- Keep code changes minimal and scoped to each task
- Update task checkbox immediately after completing each task

- Do not copy runtime context or operation guidance into implementation files or planning artifacts

This skill supports the "actions on a change" model:

content.content:
### D6 — One column definition, shared by markers, guides and accents

Measured: a marker's centre sits at exactly `depth × unit`, while a guide paints its 1px as
`[column, column + 1]`, so its visible centre is `column + 0.5` — every marker in the layer,
bullets and block icons alike, is half a pixel left of its own guide. Separately, a bullet
centres on its text rect's geometric centre while a block icon sits about 5px above it, so the
two kinds do not share a vertical rule.

Both are resolved by making the column — horizontal and vertical — one value that the guide
gradient, the marker offset and the accent layers all derive from, rather than three call sites
that agree by convention. This is the standing rule doc 11 draws from Experiment 5b's three
near-identical bugs: when two things must move together, make it impossible to change one
without the other.

### D7 — Remove the settings

The demo build's `listLayout` and `listBullet` dropdowns and their persisted fields go. They
existed to make the comparison possible, the comparison happened, and keeping them would mean
committing to four rendering combinations.

- - - - - - 
=== group 3: current list CSS ===
 *
 * A list line reserves no gutter of its own — its native marker already
 * occupies one — so `--to-marker-gutter` does not appear in this calc. It IS
 * set on the line (`lineDecoration`), because the experimental marker-column
 * rules below size the marker span to it and a fallback literal here would be
 * a second copy of `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` to keep in step by hand. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  margin-left: calc(var(--to-supp-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit)) !important;
}

/*
 * EXPERIMENTAL list geometry (`ListLayout`/`ListBullet`, see
 * docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md). Everything below hangs off a
 * class the decoration puts on LIST-ITEM LINES ONLY, so both gates — outline
 * mode, and "lists only" — come from the decoration itself and these rules
 * need no second condition. With the settings at their defaults no class is
 * emitted and none of this applies.
 *
 * The whole approach is to set the variables Obsidian's own list layout reads,
 * rather than to fight the boxes it produces. Measured (research doc, E1/E3):
 * `--list-indent` drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width` on each
 * `.cm-indent`, so pushing our own unit into it retargets every list level at
 * once.
 *
 * It does NOT carry the hanging indent with it, which an earlier version of
 * this comment claimed. Obsidian derives that from a live measurement, cached
 * per line and invalidated only by a text change or a DOM mutation its own
 * observer sees — `childList`, `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes,
 * which is all a decoration changes. So a `--list-indent` change at runtime
 * (turning outline mode on for an open note) leaves the old wrap column in
 * place until a note switch or reopen. And the measurement takes the end of
 * the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box, so with the marker
 * span sized to the gutter below, a wrapped row lands one gutter left of its
 * own item's text even when it is fresh. Both are measured, both are why the
 * `lists-on-the-outline-grid` change states this pair itself instead of
 * reading Obsidian's.
 *
 * `rem`, not the `em`-based value Obsidian ships: `--list-indent` resolves
 * where it is used, and a heading inside a list item would inflate an `em`
 * unit — the Experiment 1 bug, reachable through a new door.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-list-grid {
  --list-indent: var(--to-decor-unit);
  /*
   * Obsidian draws its indent guide as `border-inline-end` on a 1px-wide
   * absolutely-positioned `::before`, so the visible line sits ONE PIXEL RIGHT
   * of wherever that pseudo starts — while our own gradient paints its 1px at
   * exactly `depth * unit`. A 0 offset therefore leaves the two columns one
   * pixel apart, which is small enough to measure as "aligned" and still read
   * as misaligned on screen. -1px is that pixel, not a nudge.
   */
  --indentation-guide-editing-indent: -1px;
  --indentation-guide-color: var(--to-guide-color);
  --indentation-guide-color-active: var(--to-decor-accent);
}

/* Our own gradient draws the list levels instead (the decoration adds their
 * depths to `--to-guides`), so the native line would double up. Only the
 * BORDER goes: the `.cm-indent` spans themselves still do the layout, and they
 * exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is on. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-list-own-guides {
  --indentation-guide-width: 0px;
  --indentation-guide-width-active: 0px;
}

/*
 * The marker's own column. Native rendering puts the bullet a `--list-indent-
 * editing` gap right of the item's column, where every other kind centres its
 * marker ON the column and starts its text one marker gutter further right.
 *
 * Sizing the whole marker span to the gutter is what makes this
 * font-independent: the text column is then the gutter by construction rather
 * than the sum of a padding, a glyph and a space. `min-width` rather than
 * `width` so a wide ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own text out instead of
 * overlapping it.
 */
/* Scoped away from task lines exactly as the two rules below are, so the
 * exclusion is stated once instead of holding by accident. Measured: a task
 * line's checkbox does not move today either way (55.33px at both settings),
 * because Obsidian does not render a task marker inside the
 * `.cm-formatting-list` span this variable reaches — but that is a detail of

}

 * decoration itself and these rules need no second condition. Outline mode off
 * is untouched: no class, none of this.
 *
 * The approach is to set the variables Obsidian's own list layout reads rather
 * than to fight the boxes it produces. Measured (research doc, E1/E3):
 * `--list-indent` drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width` on each
 * `.cm-indent` span, so pushing our own unit into it retargets every list level
 * at once — one indent step for every kind, which is the whole change.
 *
 * `rem`, not the `em`-based value Obsidian ships: `--list-indent` resolves
 * where it is USED, so an `em` unit inflates on a heading's larger font — the
 * Experiment 1 bug, reachable through a new door.
 *
 * What this does NOT get for free is the hanging indent; see `--to-list-hang`
 * below.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-indent: var(--to-decor-unit);

  /* Our own gradient draws every list level now (`computeLineGuides` publishes
   * their depths and `activeGuideDepths` folds them in), so Obsidian's own line
   * would double up on the same column. Only its BORDER goes: the `.cm-indent`
   * spans still do the layout, and they exist only while the user's own "Show
   * indentation guides" setting is on — which stays the user's to set. */
  --indentation-guide-width: 0px;
  --indentation-guide-width-active: 0px;

  /* A bullet is a marker like any other: same weight, same colour token, so a
   * snippet retunes lists and blocks together. 0.38em against Obsidian's 0.30em
   * default — measured against the block icons' ink, which are 0.85rem at
   * stroke-width 1.5 in this same `--text-faint`. */
  --list-bullet-size: 0.38em;
}

/*
 * The marker's own column, and the text column one gutter right of it.
 *
 * Native rendering puts the bullet a `--list-indent-editing` gap right of the
 * item's column, where every other kind centres its marker ON the column. That
 * gap is what made a guide appear to run beside its bullet rather than out of
 * it. Zeroing the gap and sizing the whole marker SPAN to the gutter is what
 * makes the text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction,
 * rather than the sum of a padding, a glyph and a space.
 *
 * `min-width`, not `width`, so a wide ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own
 * text out instead of overlapping it — ordered markers therefore START on the
 * column rather than centring on it, which is the deliberate exclusion the
 * spec states.
 *
 * Task lines are excluded throughout: the checkbox lives in this same span, is
 * wider than the gutter, and is a real click target whose hit area is not this
 * layer's to reshape.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line) {
  --list-padding-inline-start: 0px;

  /*
   * The hanging indent, STATED rather than read from Obsidian's own.
   *
   * `(depth − supplementalDepth)` is the item's depth within its own list, so
   * that many units is how far Obsidian's list rendering has already carried it
   * right of the line box; one gutter more is where its text begins. Wrapped
   * rows land exactly there.
   *
   * Obsidian computes this pair itself, from a live measurement, and gets it
   * wrong here twice over (both measured, research doc): the measurement takes
   * `coordsAtPos` at the end of the marker, which is the end of the marker's
   * TEXT rather than of its padded box, so with the span sized to the gutter
   * every wrapped row landed 16px left of its own item's text; and the value is
   * cached per line and invalidated only by a text change or a DOM mutation its
   * observer sees — `childList`, `characterData`, `subtree`, never attributes,
   * which is all a decoration changes — so turning outline mode on for an open
   * note left the old wrap column in place until a note switch.
   *
   * A stated value has neither problem, and needs no measurement of ours. The
   * `!important` is what beats Obsidian's own inline style; the same rule
   * `to-decor-block` already relies on.
   */
  --to-list-hang: calc(
    (var(--to-depth, 0) - var(--to-supp-depth, 0)) * var(--to-decor-unit) +
      var(--to-marker-gutter)
  );
  padding-inline-start: var(--to-list-hang) !important;
  text-indent: calc(-1 * var(--to-list-hang)) !important;
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .cm-formatting-list {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
}

/* A zero-width bullet box centres its own `::after` — which is where the dot
 * actually lives — on the box's start edge, i.e. exactly on the column. The
 * `-`/`*`/`+` character inside is already transparent, so letting it overflow
 * costs nothing visually. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .list-bullet {
  width: 0;
}

"""
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

feat(decorations): put lists on the outline grid

Implements lists-on-the-outline-grid task groups 1-4. Outline mode had two
layouts in it: headings, paragraphs and atoms on a depth column every
`--to-decor-unit`, and lists handed back to Obsidian at 1.5x that step, with
guides on columns our grid never touched and no caret trail at all.

One grid. `--to-decor-unit` becomes a real declaration on `.cm-content` — the
single number every layer reads — and is pushed into Obsidian's own
`--list-indent` on outline-mode list lines, retargeting every list level at
once. Measured on the demo note: every marker now sits on `depth × unit` and
every text column on `depth × unit + gutter`, for headings, paragraphs, bullets,
ordered items and tasks alike. A paragraph and a list item at the same depth
share both.

One column definition. `columnExpr`/`stripeStartExpr` are the only places a
column is computed; a stripe is positioned by its own centre, which closes the
measured half-pixel where every marker sat left of its own guide because the
guide painted `[column, column + 1]`.

One guide mechanism. Obsidian's own list guide is suppressed (its border, never
the user's "Show indentation guides" setting — the `.cm-indent` spans still do
the layout) and our gradient draws every level from `listGuideDepths`. That also
lets `computePositionTrail` drop its two list-item exclusions, so the caret
trail reaches into lists for the first time.

The hanging indent is stated, not read. `(depth - supplementalDepth) * unit +
gutter` with `!important`, which fixes a measured 16px soft-wrap misalignment
(Obsidian's own measurement takes the end of the marker's TEXT, not its padded
box) and removes the stale-cache defect by having nothing to cache.

Task checkboxes join the column: the label's -4px and the input's 11.33px
inline-start margins are zeroed, and the label sized to the gutter, so the
control STARTS on the column with its width and hit area untouched.

Persisted data is normalized on load. `{ ...DEFAULT_DATA, ...loadData() }` kept
every key the file held, so deleting a setting's type left its value on the
object for the next save to write back. `normalizePluginData` picks known keys
instead — the general fix, since this is the first setting the plugin retires.

The two experimental settings are gone; this is one behaviour.

Six tests changed contract rather than breaking: three trail tests that asserted
the omission, and three e2e assertions that a pure list draws no guides and is
byte-identical to mode-off. Each is rewritten to state the new contract so the
change is visible in the diff.

Marker VERTICAL alignment is deliberately left as it was, and is the one part of
task 1.2 not delivered — see the follow-up commit's note.

Findings from `lists-on-the-outline-grid` (measurements:

- **Look for the variable before building the mechanism.** Two probes concluded that native
  list columns could only be FOLLOWED, by per-item pixel measurement, and planned a second
  rendering mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient. They were measuring the right
  thing and asking the wrong question: the columns are computed from public CSS variables, so
  they can be SET. The cost of the wrong question was a deferred feature and a planned overlay
  layer that turned out to be unnecessary.
- **Override the variable the consuming rule reads, not an intermediate one.**
  `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
  overriding `--list-indent-editing` further down does nothing — the substitution already
  happened above. Overriding `--list-padding-inline-start` itself works. `--list-indent` is
  consumed directly by `.cm-line`/`.cm-indent` and can be scoped as far down as a single line's
  own class, which is what gates all of this on outline mode with no second condition.
- **Obsidian's list hanging indent is a cached live measurement, and its cache does not watch
  attributes.** It observes `childList`, `characterData` and `subtree`, so anything that
  changes the rendered width of a list prefix through CSS alone leaves the hang stale until the
  line's text changes or the view is rebuilt. It also measures `coordsAtPos` at the end of the
  marker, which is the end of the marker's TEXT rather than of its padded box. Both are reasons
  to STATE a value the layer already knows instead of reading one back.
- **`--list-indent` is `em`-based.** Anything of ours flowing into it must be `rem`, or the
  Experiment 1 font-size bug returns through a new door.
- **A user setting can move geometry, not just paint.** With Obsidian's "Show indentation
  guides" off, the `.cm-indent` spans do not exist at all, and space-indented list levels
  change width. Any reasoning about list columns has to name which side of that setting it
  holds on.
- **`vertical-align: middle` resolves against the PARENT's x-height, which makes it
  font-size-relative in a way that bites on headings.** It is the right optical anchor for a
  small mark beside body text and the wrong one for a marker on an H1, where it drops the mark
  below the heading's own glyphs. Two marks of different size and box model may simply not
  share one numeric vertical anchor; that is worth discovering by looking rather than asserting
  in a spec.

Task groups 5 and 6 of lists-on-the-outline-grid.

The spec's vertical requirement is amended rather than left disagreeing with
the implementation. It asked for one vertical anchor across marker kinds; that
was built and reversed. `vertical-align: middle` — the optical centre of a row
of lowercase text — is right for a 6px dot and wrong for a 13.6px glyph on a
heading, because `middle` resolves against the PARENT's x-height: on an H1 the
icon dropped from 8.45px above its text-rect centre to 2.96px below, landing
under the heading's own glyphs and against the guide starting on the row
beneath. Reported from the demo build and confirmed in a screenshot. The
requirement now states a per-kind anchor and says why, with a scenario guarding
the failure mode that actually matters — a marker drifting down a taller row.

Verification. A `list-grid` fixture joins the shared corpus, so every spec that
screenshots the corpus now covers it. `56-list-grid.e2e.ts` measures rendered
positions rather than the custom properties that produce them: one unit per
level for tabs and four-spaces, marker on its column for bullets and
checkboxes, text one gutter right of the column for every kind, wrapped rows on
their own item's text column both freshly opened AND after a mode toggle, a
wide ordered marker pushing its own text out, the native guide suppressed, our
own drawn one layer per ancestor, and no contribution at all with the mode off.
It also pins the two-space residual as Obsidian's behaviour rather than a
regression of ours: the FACT stays correct, only the render does not.

Text columns come from the text nodes' own client rects, never `coordsAtPos` —
which reports the end of a marker's TEXT rather than of its box and so agreed
with the 16px soft-wrap defect this change fixes. Fixtures are one short note
per shape: CM6 renders only the viewport, and a fixture longer than the window
silently drops its tail, which cost a round of confusing failures.

The Minimal pass is done: Minimal sets `--list-indent: 2em` itself and puts its
own margin on list lines, and the per-line rules win both — grid intact,
bullets on their columns, wrapped rows under their own text.

design.md's open question is settled as documentation only: a notice would fire
on a condition the user cannot act on from inside the note and that is
Obsidian's behaviour rather than the plugin's. README gains a "Known
limitations" section for the two- and three-space case and the indent-guide
setting dependency.

docs/research/11 gains the carried-forward findings — look for the variable
before building the mechanism; override the variable the consuming rule reads;
Obsidian's list hang is a cached measurement whose cache ignores attributes;
`--list-indent` is em-based; a user setting can move geometry; and
`vertical-align: middle` is font-size-relative in a way that bites on headings.
docs/research/12 closes three parking-lot entries and reopens the
vertical-alignment one with the reversal.

content.text:
## Implementation complete

**29 of 30 tasks.** `openspec validate --strict` passes; 854 unit tests, lint, typecheck, and 22/22 e2e spec files green. Pushed as `7b753df` + `fbb3c32`.

The guide highlighting you asked about now works in lists — that was two deleted conditions in `computePositionTrail`, correct only once list levels had a column to draw on.

Measured on the demo note, every marker sits on `depth × unit` and every text column on `depth × unit + gutter` — headings, paragraphs, bullets, ordered items and tasks alike. A paragraph and a list item at the same depth share both.

## Your report, and what I got wrong

You caught the icons being too low and overlapping the guides. That was mine, from unifying the vertical anchor on `vertical-align: middle`. It resolves against the **parent's** x-height, so on an H1 it dropped the icon from 8.45px above its text-rect centre to 2.96px *below* — under the heading's glyphs, hard against the guide starting on the next row. Reverted; screenshot confirms icons are back where they were.

**So one task didn't land as specified.** The spec required one vertical anchor across marker kinds. A 13.6px outline glyph in the text flow and a 6px dot in a flex box don't read as aligned at one offset, and no CSS anchor serves both across font sizes. The bullet keeps the optical centre (fixing your earlier "a tad too high"), the icon keeps `baseline`, and they differ ~7px on a body row. I amended the requirement to say that, with a scenario guarding the failure that matters — a marker drifting down a taller row — rather than leave the spec claiming something false. **Worth your eyes**: whether that 7px reads as wrong is a judgement I shouldn't make alone.

**Task 6.7, the by-hand real-vault pass, is unchecked** — it's yours. The demo note and the whole corpus are built into the vault.

## Two things worth knowing

**Minimal passes.** It sets `--list-indent: 2em` and its own margin on list lines; our per-line rules win both — grid intact, wrapped rows under their own text.

**I lost and restored a small edit of yours.** The three-level list you'd typed into `Journal/2026-07-10.md` got reverted by a suite run. I've put it back exactly; drop it if it was scratch. Your `data.json` (with `markerHighlight: lineage`) is untouched in the working tree, deliberately uncommitted.

Also settled: the two-space residual is documented in a README "Known limitations" section rather than surfaced as a notice — it's Obsidian's behaviour on a condition you can't act on from inside the note. An e2e test pins it as Obsidian's, not ours regressing: the tree depth stays correct, only the render doesn't.

content.text:
Fixed and pushed as `07a5da8`.

**The failure was my assertion, not the rendering.** A task checkbox's text column measured 20.33 against an asserted 20.00. I reproduced it locally under mobile emulation — and it's also why the Linux desktop runner failed, since a checkbox's intrinsic width is the platform's, not this layer's.

The spec deliberately asks only two things of the markers whose width this layer *doesn't* set — a checkbox and a wide ordered number: **start on the column, never overlap the item's own text.** It doesn't ask for a fixed text column, because the label is sized with `min-width`, so a control wider than the gutter pushing its own text out is the designed behaviour — identical to what `10. ` does. I'd written the test against a pixel the macOS font happened to produce rather than against the contract. Now it asserts the contract, and I gave `9. ninth` the same treatment for the same reason: it fits the gutter in both fonts I've measured, but a glyph's width is the font's business.

Verified on the whole decorations group under mobile emulation, not just the one spec.

**One thing I want to flag rather than bury.** The first full desktop re-run after that fix had two *different* failures — `forward mouse drag crossing a boundary` and `live drag stability`, both in `63-selection-visual-treatment`. They passed on an isolated re-run and passed again on a second full suite (22/22, just now). Both are mouse-drag tests, which this repo's helpers already document as the class most sensitive to machine load, and my box has been launching Obsidian repeatedly for hours. So: most likely load, and nothing in this change touches drag or paragraph selection chrome.

But I'm telling you because this repo's own lesson is that a flaky test can be a real bug wearing a timing costume, and "it passed the second time" isn't proof. If CI shows them failing on a clean runner, that's the signal to take seriously — I'd start with whether the list-line `padding-inline-start`/`text-indent` `!important` rules interact with the selection chrome's `--to-selected-left`.

centring, justified as "the checkbox is wider than the gutter" — measured, it is not: 16px
against a 20px gutter. Nothing was stopping it centring, and starting it there is exactly what
real use reported, a checkbox sitting nearer its text than the bullets above and below it in a
mixed list.

A wide ordered marker genuinely can exceed the gutter (`10. ` measures 28px), so centring it
would push it left of the column its own text has to clear. That one, and only that one, still
starts on its column."""

2	
3	See proposal.md for motivation, and
4	[docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md)
5	for the measurements every decision below rests on — taken live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the
6	e2e harness, then reviewed by hand in a demo build whose two experimental settings this change
7	removes.
8	
9	Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:
10	
11	1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
12	   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on
13	   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
14	   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.
15	2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
16	   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
17	   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
18	   quantum that is not the Tab size.
19	3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
20	   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
21	   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
22	4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
23	   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
24	   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
25	   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
26	   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.

28	## Goals / Non-Goals
29	
30	**Goals:**
31	
32	- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
33	- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
34	  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
35	- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
36	  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
37	  one of ours.
38	
39	**Non-Goals:**
40	
41	- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
42	  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
43	- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
44	  three-space indentation). See Risks.
45	- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
46	  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
47	  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.

50	
51	### D1 — Set the variables Obsidian reads, rather than positioning list lines ourselves
52	
53	Scope `--list-indent` (and the guide and marker-gap variables) to `.cm-line.to-decor-list`, the
54	class the decoration already puts on list-item lines. Both gates — outline mode, and lists only
55	— then come from the decoration itself and the CSS needs no second condition. Confirmed live:
56	an outline-mode note retargets and a non-outline note open beside it is byte-identical to
57	stock.
58	
59	*Alternatives considered.* Measuring each item's bullet and drawing overlays at those
60	coordinates (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) was the approach two earlier
61	probes concluded was the only one available. It is a second rendering mechanism with its own
62	reflow bookkeeping, and Experiment 2b replaced exactly that with the measurement-free gradient
63	the layer now rests on. Forcing a width onto `.cm-hmd-list-indent` per line was also built and
64	measured: the geometry is right and the caret round-trips, but it desynchronises Obsidian's
65	hanging indent (see D3) and needs a per-line custom property where a single variable does.
66	
67	### D2 — Draw the list guides ourselves; do not share with Obsidian's
68	
69	Suppress the native indent guide on our list lines (its width, not the user's setting, so the
70	`.cm-indent` spans that carry layout still exist) and lift `computeLineGuides`' list-item
71	exclusion so the existing gradient draws every level.
72	
73	Keeping the native guide was the cheaper option and was rejected on two measured grounds. It
74	disappears entirely when the user turns "Show indentation guides" off, so list levels would
75	lose their guides for a reason unrelated to outline mode. And it accents only ONE level — the
76	caret's own, via `.cm-active-indent` — where the trail accents the whole ancestor chain, so the
77	position indicator would still be missing inside lists, which is one of the things this change
78	exists to fix.
79	
80	`LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths in a field of their own rather than
81	merged into `guideDepths`. The walk publishes them unconditionally and the consumer combines
82	them, which keeps the fact independent of any rendering decision and keeps the per-`Text`
83	fact cache correct without a second key.
84	
85	### D3 — State the hanging indent; do not read Obsidian's
86	
87	Write `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent` on our list lines from
88	`(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter`, with `!important` — the rule this codebase
89	already relies on for `to-decor-block`, where an important stylesheet declaration beats
90	Obsidian's non-important inline style.
91	
92	Two measured defects close together. Obsidian derives the hang from `coordsAtPos` at the end of
93	the marker, which reports the end of the marker's TEXT rather than the end of its padded box:
94	with the marker span sized to the gutter, every soft-wrapped list row lands 16px left of its

96	cached against attributes the observer does not watch, retargeting the grid at runtime — which

98	reopened. A stated value has neither problem: measured exact in both the freshly-opened and
99	the toggled-on case.
100	
101	*Alternative considered and rejected.* Provoking the `childList` mutation Obsidian's cache does
102	watch (append an empty hidden span to each list line, remove it again) was built and confirmed
103	to work, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. It was backed out: this repo's own
104	lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU
105	mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a
106	judgement rather than a measurement. Stating the value removes the need entirely.
107	
108	### D4 — The bullet is Obsidian's, positioned and weighted by us
109

111	a real element on the real column, it already carries the collapsed/hover states and the

116	
117	Position: zero `--list-padding-inline-start`, a zero-width bullet box so its absolutely

5	In outline mode, the distance between one tree level and the next SHALL be the same for every

22	Obsidian does not resolve renders its list levels at columns this requirement does not
23	control, with the mode on or off.

56	
57	A LIST ITEM takes its contribution in two parts, which together put it on that same grid:

59	non-list-item ancestors above the nearest list root, plus the item's own depth WITHIN its
60	list, which Obsidian's own list rendering supplies once the outline unit is the unit it
61	renders a list level at. The plugin SHALL retarget that native rendering by supplying the
62	unit, and SHALL state the item's own hanging indent; it SHALL NOT reposition a list item by
63	overriding native rendering line by line.
64	
65	Nodes at the same tree depth SHALL receive the same indentation contribution regardless of
66	whether their depth is encoded via heading level, list indentation, or paragraph adjacency,
67	AND regardless of whether the line is currently rendered as plain text or as an opaque widget.

Both fixed and pushed as `4b7bc5a`.

**Ordered numbers** had exactly the checkbox defect — span starting at the column, so the glyphs sat right of centre. A number can't shrink its box the way a bullet does (the glyphs *are* the mark), so the painted span is shifted left with `transform`, moving the ink without moving the box its text follows.

I shifted by **half the gutter, not half the number's own width** — and that's worth flagging, because it means `10.` and `100.` aren't perfectly centred. I built the by-own-width version first and measured it out: `1.` centres exactly, but `10.` then reaches 14px left of the column and `100.` 19px, leaving nothing for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px there and can't go further without crossing the parent guide one unit away. The fixed shift centres a single digit exactly, leans wider numbers right into space their own text already reserves, and gives the list **one left edge** — which reads as a column rather than as ragged centring. If you'd rather have every number truly centred and accept a cramped chevron on multi-digit lists, that's a one-line change.

**The chevron overlap** was the same root cause: Obsidian renders it with its right edge on the content origin — harmless while markers began *right* of that origin, straight through them once centred. test(e2e): assert the ordered-marker RULE, not the font it was written on

ordered marker's centre: 24.18 against a column of 24.

The rendering is right and the assertion was wrong, for the third time in this
change and for the same reason each time — a pixel that one font happened to
produce, asserted as though it were the contract.

The rule is a fixed half-gutter shift. A number centres on its column only while
its glyphs fit INSIDE the gutter, because the box is `min-width: gutter`; once
they exceed it the box grows and the number leans right by half the excess,
which is the designed behaviour for a wide marker. `1. ` measures 18.4px in the
bundled theme on macOS and 20.36px on CI's Linux font, so the lean starts one
digit earlier there. Nothing was broken; my test just encoded macOS's font
metrics as the requirement.

It now asserts the rule directly — every number's box starts exactly half a
gutter left of its column, which is font-independent and is what makes the left
edge shared — and keeps the centring as a bounded consequence: never left of the
column, never more than half a gutter right of it.

The spec and design said "a single digit centres exactly" and now say what is
actually guaranteed: a number narrow enough to fit the gutter is centred, which
numbers those are depends on the font, and the invariants that hold regardless
are the shared left edge and never overlapping its own text.

Pushed as `ddb2c1c`. The rendering was right; my assertion was wrong — **for the third time in this change, and the same mistake each time**: encoding a pixel one font happened to produce as if it were the contract.

The rule is a fixed half-gutter shift. A number centres on its column only while its glyphs fit *inside* the gutter, because the box is `min-width: gutter` — once they exceed it the box grows and the number leans right by half the excess, which is the designed behaviour for a wide marker. `1. ` measures **18.4px on macOS and 20.36px on CI's Linux font**, so the lean simply starts one digit earlier there. The test now asserts the rule directly — every number's box starts exactly half a gutter left of its column, which is font-independent and is what makes the left edge shared — and keeps the centring as a bounded consequence: never left of the column, never more than half a gutter right of it. The spec and design said "a single digit centres exactly" and now say what's actually guaranteed.

I should have caught this pattern after the second time. The tell was there: every assertion that reduced to "a glyph is N pixels wide" has failed off my machine, and every one that stated a relationship between computed columns has held. Worth naming as a lesson for `docs/research/11` if it survives one more round.

## 1. The shared column definition (design D6)

- [x] 1.1 Establish one source for a depth's column: the unit, the marker's own centre offset,
      and the gradient's 1px stop all derive from it, so a marker's visible centre and its
      guide's visible centre coincide by construction rather than by convention. Fix the
      measured half-pixel: markers sit at `depth × unit`, the guide paints `[column, column+1]`.
- [x] 1.2 Establish one vertical anchor for markers across kinds — measured today, a bullet
      centres on its text rect while a block icon sits ~5px above it. Decide the anchor against
      the optical centre of a text row (a rect centre reads ~1.5px high), apply it to synthetic
      markers and the native bullet alike, and fold in `docs/research/12`'s existing
      "vertical-alignment polish" entry for the widget-atom icons while the rule is being set.
- [x] 1.3 Declare `--to-decor-unit` as a real value rather than a CSS fallback, so
      `--list-indent` and everything else read one number. No user setting in this change.
- [x] 1.4 E2e-assert that a marker's centre and its own guide's PAINTED centre agree, in both
      bundled themes (`56-list-grid.e2e.ts`). Not unit-tested: the derivation lives in
      `decorations.ts`, which imports `obsidian` and so cannot be loaded by vitest — and the
      rendered stripe is the thing worth asserting anyway, this layer's whole history being of
      computations that were internally consistent and rendered wrong.

## 2. Pure decoration facts

- [x] 2.1 `LineGuideFact` carries the active list-item ancestor depths in their own field,
      emitted unconditionally (content lines and gap lines alike) so a blank line inside a list
      keeps its guides continuous. Already present on the demo branch — review it against the
      spec rather than rewriting it.
- [x] 2.2 Unit-test the new field: a pure list, a list under a heading, a list under a
      paragraph, a multi-line item's continuation, a gap line between items, and a non-list
      child of a list item.
- [x] 2.3 Remove `computePositionTrail`'s two `isListItem` exclusions (`'full'`'s `continue`,
      `'lineage'`'s rung filter) so the trail steps one level per ancestor whatever its kind.
- [x] 2.4 Rewrite the three trail tests that assert the old omission — "runs the segment at the
      shallower non-list column, through the list levels", "accents only the non-list ancestor
      in the guides style", "draws no segment anywhere in a pure list, in either style" —
      against the new contract, and add a pure-list lineage case.

## 3. List geometry

- [x] 3.1 Emit the list line's own tree depth alongside its supplemental depth, so the CSS can
      state the hanging indent.
- [x] 3.2 Push the unit into `--list-indent`, scoped to outline-mode list lines. Verify a
      second note without outline mode, open at the same time, is byte-identical to stock.
- [x] 3.3 State the hanging indent from `(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter` with
      `!important`, replacing Obsidian's measured value (design D3).
- [x] 3.4 Put the marker on its column: zero the marker gap, zero-width bullet box, marker span
      sized to the gutter with `min-width`. Exclude task lines from CENTRING — a checkbox is
      wider than the gutter and is a click target — and scope every rule that implements the
      exclusion the same way, so it is stated once rather than holding by accident.
- [x] 3.5 CENTRE a task checkbox on its own depth column, like the bullet it sits among,
      without changing its width or hit area. (Landed first as "start on the column", which
      real use reported as a checkbox sitting nearer its text than the bullets around it; the
      "wider than the gutter" reason for not centring was measured false — 16px against a 20px
      gutter. See design D5.)
- [x] 3.6 Set the bullet weight to `0.38em`, colour token unchanged.
- [x] 3.8 Bring an ordered number onto the column too, by a fixed half-gutter shift rather than
      half its own width (which leaves no room for the fold chevron), so a single digit centres
      exactly and every number in a list shares one left edge.
- [x] 3.9 Move the fold chevron off the marker it belongs to: Obsidian renders it with its right
      edge on the content origin, which is now the marker's own centre. `--list-bullet-end-padding`
      is not the lever — measured at three values, the glyph never moved (design D8).
- [x] 3.7 Suppress Obsidian's own list-guide line on those lines — its width only, never the
      user's "Show indentation guides" setting — and include the list-ancestor depths in the

## 4. Remove the experimental settings

- [x] 4.1 Delete `ListLayout`/`ListBullet`, their `PluginData` fields and defaults, the
      `DecorationSource` members, the plugin accessors, and both settings-tab entries
      (declarative and pre-1.13 fallback).
- [x] 4.2 Delete the classes and CSS branches that existed only to switch between variants; the
      remaining rules hang off `to-decor-list` alone.
- [x] 4.3 Normalize persisted data on load: build `this.data` by picking the known keys rather
      than spreading whatever `loadData()` returns, so a removed setting actually disappears
      instead of surviving on the object and being written back by the next `saveData`

## 5. Specs and docs

- [x] 5.1 Fold the two delta specs into `openspec/specs/` on archive; until then keep them

- [x] 5.2 Update `docs/research/12-decoration-follow-ups.md`: close "shrinking only our own

- [x] 5.3 Add the carried-forward findings from
      `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` to `docs/research/11-decoration-lessons.md`:

      rule reads, not an intermediate one; Obsidian's list hang is a cached measurement whose
      cache ignores attributes; `--list-indent` is `em`-based so anything of ours flowing into

- [x] 5.4 Record the residuals where a user will meet them, not only in research: two- and
      three-space files, and space-indented files with indent guides off. Settle design.md's

## 6. Verification

- [x] 6.1 Grow the shared fixture corpus with a list-geometry fixture: tab / four-space /
      two-space nesting, ordered across the 9→10 boundary, tasks, a blank line inside a list, a
      soft-wrapping item at two levels, and a list attached to a paragraph.
- [x] 6.2 E2e: every list level steps by one unit and equals a same-depth heading's column;
      guides render one line per level on that same grid; a bullet sits on its own guide.
- [x] 6.3 E2e: a soft-wrapping nested item's wrapped rows align with its own text — both on a
      freshly opened note AND after turning outline mode on for a note already open, which is
      the case a measured hang got wrong.
- [x] 6.4 E2e: outline mode off renders stock, for a pure list and for a mixed document.
- [x] 6.5 E2e: the trail reaches every list level, and every setting combination leaves a
      list's geometry unchanged.
- [x] 6.6 Screenshot the full corpus in both bundled themes (specs 50/51/52 do this for every
      fixture, and the corpus now includes `list-grid`), and the Minimal pass: Minimal sets
      `--list-indent: 2em` itself and puts a `--list-edit-offset` margin on list lines, and our
      per-line rules win both — grid intact, bullets on their columns, wrapped rows under their
      own text.
- [ ] 6.7 Real-vault pass by hand over `test-vault/`, including
      `Notes/List decoration demo.md`. This is the gate, not the fixtures — every bug in this
      layer's history was found here and none by the synthetic corpus.
- [x] 6.8 Full suite green: 854 unit tests, lint, typecheck, 22/22 desktop e2e spec files.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Trail rendering through list nesting uses the same columns as every other level

Where the current node's ancestor chain runs through list nesting, the trail SHALL render at
those levels exactly as it renders at any other: a segment on that ancestor's own depth
column, drawn by the same mechanism, in the same weight and colour as a segment at a heading's
level. A list ancestor SHALL NOT be skipped, and no level of the chain SHALL be left without a
segment on the grounds of its kind.

This SUPERSEDES the previous omission, which required list levels to be positioned on
Obsidian's own native list columns or else render nothing. That omission existed because list
levels had no column this plugin could address; `outline-decorations` now puts every list
level on the same grid as every other kind, so the column exists and the trail uses it.

A list ancestor's own MARKER continues to be accented like any other ancestor's, whether or not
a segment is drawn at its level.

#### Scenario: A trail through a list draws at every level

- **WHEN** the caret is inside a list nested several levels deep under a heading, with a trail
  style active
- **THEN** a segment renders at each list level's own column as well as at the heading's, all
  on the same grid and in the same weight

#### Scenario: A pure list shows its levels through segments and bullets together

- **WHEN** the caret is inside a deeply nested pure list — no non-list ancestor anywhere — and
  both settings are at a state that renders
- **THEN** each ancestor level renders its segment, and each ancestor list item renders its
  native bullet accented

#### Scenario: The lineage route runs unbroken into a list

- **WHEN** the caret is on a list item several levels inside a list that itself sits under two
  headings, and the guide setting is `lineage`
- **THEN** the accented route steps in one level per ancestor from the outline root to the
  caret, with no level of the chain missing and no gap where the headings hand over to the
  list

### Requirement: Position indicators never change layout geometry

Enabling, disabling, or switching any position-indicator setting SHALL NOT change any line's
indentation, marker gutter, marker size or position, guide column, or text position. Only colors
and other purely visual attributes SHALL differ between settings. This SHALL hold for list items
exactly as for every other kind: a list item's own indentation, bullet position and text
position SHALL be identical at every setting value.

#### Scenario: Toggling indicators never reflows text

- **WHEN** either setting is changed to any other one of its values
- **THEN** every line's rendered indentation and text position, and every marker's size and
  position, are identical to what they were before the change

#### Scenario: Turning everything off restores the base rendering

- **WHEN** both settings are `off`
- **THEN** the note renders exactly as the base decoration layers alone render it

#### Scenario: A list's geometry is constant across every setting

- **WHEN** the caret is inside a nested list and the settings are cycled through every
  combination
- **THEN** every list line's indentation, bullet column and text column are unchanged
  throughout

## Why

Outline mode renders headings, paragraphs and atoms on one grid — a depth column every
`--to-decor-unit`, a marker centred on that column, a guide descending from it — and then
hands lists back to Obsidian. The result is two layouts in one document: a list level steps
`2.25em` where every other level steps `1.5rem`, a list's guides sit on native columns that
our own grid never touches, and a list ancestor gets no caret trail at all because there is no
column of ours to draw it on.

The experiment series left it that way deliberately, and two later probes concluded that
native list columns could only be FOLLOWED, by per-item pixel measurement — a second rendering
mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient the whole layer rests on
([docs/research/14](../../../docs/research/14-experiment-position-indicators.md), finding 3).
That conclusion was right about the mechanism it examined and wrong about the problem.
Obsidian computes list columns from public CSS variables, so they can be SET rather than
followed. [docs/research/16](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md) measures the
whole surface against a running Obsidian 1.13.4 and confirms it: one variable puts every tab-
or four-space-indented list level on our own unit, with Obsidian's own hanging indent
re-deriving itself, and a second puts its guides on our columns. No measurement, no second
mechanism.

A demo build of exactly that was reviewed by hand and accepted. This change makes it the
behaviour.

## What Changes

- **List levels step by the outline unit.** `--to-decor-unit` is pushed into Obsidian's own
  `--list-indent` on outline-mode list lines, so a list level and a heading level are the same
  distance. **BREAKING** for the rendering contract: a pure list no longer renders
  byte-identical to outline-mode-off.
- **Our own guides draw every list level.** The native list guide is switched off on those
  lines and `computeLineGuides`' list-item exclusion is lifted, so a list level's guide is the
  same gradient, the same colour and the same column as a heading's.
- **The caret trail reaches into lists.** With list levels on the grid,
  `computePositionTrail`'s two `isListItem` exclusions are removed and the position indicator
  accents list levels like any other — closing the omission
  `hierarchy-position-indicators` currently states as a requirement.
- **A list marker sits on its own depth column**, with the item's text at the marker gutter,
  so a guide descends out of its bullet the way it descends out of a block marker.
- **We write the hanging indent instead of reading Obsidian's.** Measured: the marker gutter
  makes every soft-wrapped list row land 16px left of its own item's text, because
  `coordsAtPos` — and therefore Obsidian's own measurement — reports the end of the marker's
  TEXT rather than the end of its padded box. Writing the pair from
  `(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter` is exact, and being a `calc()` it also removes
  the stale-cache defect where a live change to `--list-indent` left the old wrap column in
  place.
- **The bullet gets the weight of a marker**: `--list-bullet-size` `0.38em`, measured against
  the block icons' ink; the colour token is unchanged so lists and blocks retune together.
- **Markers and guides share one column definition.** Measured: every marker's centre sits at
  exactly `depth × unit` while the guide paints its 1px as `[column, column + 1]`, so every
  marker — bullets and block icons alike — is half a pixel left of the line it belongs to. A
  list bullet also uses a different vertical anchor from a block icon (the text rect's centre
  against roughly 5px above it). Both are resolved here, from one shared definition rather
  than per-consumer.
- **No new settings.** The demo build's two experimental dropdowns are removed; this is one
  behaviour, not an option.

Deliberately NOT in scope, and recorded as residuals rather than fixed: files indented with
two or three spaces (Obsidian quantises only a tab or exactly four spaces, so their levels are
misaligned with the plugin disabled too, and our guides make that more visible rather than
less); the dependency of space-indented files on Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides"
setting, which controls whether the spans that carry list layout exist at all; and making the
indent unit a user-facing setting, which belongs with the wider layer-configurability item.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None. This changes how existing layers render, not what the plugin can do.

### Modified Capabilities

- `outline-decorations`: the pure-list byte-identical requirement is replaced by a one-grid
  requirement; indentation, guides and markers gain list-item cases; the hanging indent
  becomes ours to state.
- `hierarchy-position-indicators`: "Trail rendering through list nesting uses native list
  chrome or is omitted" is replaced — list levels now have a column of ours and render the
  trail like any other level.

## Impact

- `src/plugin/decorate.ts` — `LineGuideFact` carries the list-item ancestor depths;
  `computePositionTrail` stops excluding list ancestors. Pure functions, unit-tested.
- `src/plugin/decorations.ts` — list lines emit their own depth and the classes the new CSS
  hangs off; the guide background includes list levels.
- `src/plugin/mode-registry.ts`, `src/plugin/main.ts` — the two experimental settings and
  their persisted fields are removed.
- `styles.css` — the list rules: the unit, the guide handover, the marker column, the hanging
  indent, the bullet weight, and the shared column definition markers and guides both read.
- `tests/decorate.test.ts` — three trail tests assert the omission being closed and are
  rewritten to assert the new behaviour; new coverage for the list-ancestor guide depths.
- `e2e/specs/50–55` — the decoration suites gain list-grid cases; the fixture corpus grows a
  list-geometry fixture. `test-vault/Notes/List decoration demo.md` stays as a real-vault
  fixture.
- No change to the document model, the parse, any structural operation, or anything written to
  disk. The layer stays a pure rendering projection.
