content.content:
* occupies one — so `--to-marker-gutter` does not appear in this calc. It IS
 * set on the line (`lineDecoration`), because the experimental marker-column
 * rules below size the marker span to it and a fallback literal here would be
 * a second copy of `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` to keep in step by hand. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  margin-left: calc(var(--to-supp-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit)) !important;
}

/*
 * LIST GEOMETRY (lists-on-the-outline-grid, docs/research/16). Everything here
 * hangs off `to-decor-list`, a class the decoration puts on LIST-ITEM LINES
 * ONLY, so both gates — outline mode, and "lists only" — come from the
 * decoration itself and these rules need no second condition. Outline mode off
 * is untouched: no class, none of this.
 *
 * The approach is to set the variables Obsidian's own list layout reads rather
 * than to fight the boxes it produces. Measured (research doc, E1/E3):
 * `--list-indent` drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width` on each
 * `.cm-indent` span, so pushing our own unit into it retargets every list level
 * at once — one indent step for every kind, which is the whole change.
 *
 * `rem`, not the `em`-based value Obsidian ships: `--list-indent` resolves
 * where it is USED, so an `em` unit inflates on a heading's larger font — the
 * Experiment 1 bug, reachable through a new door.
 *
 * What this does NOT get for free is the hanging indent; see `--to-list-hang`
 * below.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-indent: var(--to-decor-unit);

  /* Our own gradient draws every list level now (`computeLineGuides` publishes
   * their depths and `activeGuideDepths` folds them in), so Obsidian's own line
   * would double up on the same column. Only its BORDER goes: the `.cm-indent`
   * spans still do the layout, and they exist only while the user's own "Show
   * indentation guides" setting is on — which stays the user's to set. */
  --indentation-guide-width: 0px;
  --indentation-guide-width-active: 0px;

  /* A bullet is a marker like any other: same weight, same colour token, so a
   * snippet retunes lists and blocks together. 0.38em against Obsidian's 0.30em
   * default — measured against the block icons' ink, which are 0.85rem at
   * stroke-width 1.5 in this same `--text-faint`. */
  --list-bullet-size: 0.38em;
}

/*
 * The marker's own column, and the text column one gutter right of it.
 *
 * Native rendering puts the bullet a `--list-indent-editing` gap right of the
 * item's column, where every other kind centres its marker ON the column. That
 * gap is what made a guide appear to run beside its bullet rather than out of
 * it. Zeroing the gap and sizing the whole marker SPAN to the gutter is what
 * makes the text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction,
 * rather than the sum of a padding, a glyph and a space.
 *
 * `min-width`, not `width`, so a wide ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own
 * text out instead of overlapping it — ordered markers therefore START on the
 * column rather than centring on it, which is the deliberate exclusion the
 * spec states.
 *
 * Task lines are excluded throughout: the checkbox lives in this same span, is
 * wider than the gutter, and is a real click target whose hit area is not this
 * layer's to reshape.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-padding-inline-start: 0px;

  /*
   * The hanging indent, STATED rather than read from Obsidian's own.
   *
   * `(depth − supplementalDepth)` is the item's depth within its own list, so
   * that many units is how far Obsidian's list rendering has already carried it
   * right of the line box; one gutter more is where its text begins. Wrapped
   * rows land exactly there.
   *
   * Obsidian computes this pair itself, from a live measurement, and gets it
   * wrong here twice over (both measured, research doc): the measurement takes
   * `coordsAtPos` at the end of the marker, which is the end of the marker's
   * TEXT rather than of its padded box, so with the span sized to the gutter
   * every wrapped row landed 16px left of its own item's text; and the value is
   * cached per line and invalidated only by a text change or a DOM mutation its
   * observer sees — `childList`, `characterData`, `subtree`, never attributes,
   * which is all a decoration changes — so turning outline mode on for an open
   * note left the old wrap column in place until a note switch.
   *
   * A stated value has neither problem, and needs no measurement of ours. The
   * `!important` is what beats Obsidian's own inline style; the same rule
   * `to-decor-block` already relies on.
   */
  --to-list-hang: calc(
    (var(--to-depth, 0) - var(--to-supp-depth, 0)) * var(--to-decor-unit) +
      var(--to-marker-gutter)
  );
  padding-inline-start: var(--to-list-hang) !important;
  text-indent: calc(-1 * var(--to-list-hang)) !important;
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .cm-formatting-list {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
}

/*
 * An ordered item's number is a node marker like any other, so it centres on
 * the column too. It cannot do that by shrinking its box the way a bullet does
 * — the glyphs ARE the mark, and their width is the font's and the number's —
 * so the box keeps its layout position (text stays at `column + gutter`) and
 * the painted glyphs are shifted half their own width left. `transform` is what
 * makes that free: it moves the ink without moving anything around it.
 *
 * The shift is half the GUTTER, not half the number's own width. Centring each
 * number on its own width was tried and measured: `1. ` centres exactly, but
 * `10. ` reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, and nothing is left
 * for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px on that side and cannot go further
 * without crossing the parent level's guide. A fixed shift centres a
 * single-digit marker exactly, leans wider ones right — into their own text's
 * space, which `min-width` has already accounted for — and gives every number
 * in a list ONE left edge, which reads as a column rather than as ragged
 * centring.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .cm-formatting-list-ol {
  transform: translateX(calc(var(--to-marker-gutter) / -2));
}

/*
 * Obsidian's fold chevron on a list line renders with its right edge ON the
 * item's own content origin — which, now that a marker is CENTRED on the column
 * rather than starting right of it, is straight through that marker: measured,
 * the glyph occupies [column-10, column] while a bullet's dot occupies
 * [column-3, column+3].
 *
 * `--list-bullet-end-padding` looks like the lever and is not: raising it grows
 * the indicator's box to the right (its `inset-inline-end` compensates by
 * exactly as much), leaving the glyph where it was. Measured at 1.3rem, 2rem
 * and 2.6rem — the glyph stayed at [14, 24] in all three.
 *
 * So the glyph is moved directly. It is absolutely positioned, so a transform
 * moves the ink and disturbs no layout. Half a gutter clears the widest centred
 * mark (a checkbox, half of it 8px) and 2px more keeps it off the ordered
 * marker's own left edge, while staying clear of the parent level's guide one
 * unit away.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list
  .cm-fold-indicator
  .collapse-indicator {
  transform: translateX(calc(var(--to-marker-gutter) / -2 - 2px));
}

/* A zero-width bullet box centres its own `::after` — which is where the dot
 * actually lives — on the box's start edge, i.e. exactly on the column. The
 * `-`/`*`/`+` character inside is already transparent, so letting it overflow
 * costs nothing visually. */
/*
 * A task line's marker is a checkbox, not a bullet, but it is the same THING —
 * the mark that stands for the node — so it takes the same column, CENTRED on
 * it exactly as a bullet's dot is. Natively it starts 7.33px right of the
 * column (the label's own -4px and the input's own inline-start margin,
 * measured), which in a mixed list puts a checkbox visibly nearer its text than
 * the bullets above and below it.
 *
 * Zeroing both margins and then pulling the control back by half its own width
 * centres it. `--checkbox-size` is Obsidian's own variable for that width, so
 * this follows a theme that resizes the control instead of assuming 16px.
 * Sizing the LABEL to the marker gutter keeps the item's text at
 * `column + gutter`, the same text column every other kind uses; the control's
 * own width, and therefore its hit area, is untouched.
 *
 * An earlier version of this rule started the checkbox on the column instead,
 * on the stated grounds that a checkbox is "wider than the gutter". Measured,
 * it is not — 16px against a 20px gutter — so there was never anything stopping
 * it centring, and starting it there was the misalignment reported from real
 * use. A wide ordered marker genuinely can exceed the gutter (`10. ` measures
 * 28px), which is why that one, and only that one, still starts on its column.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list.HyperMD-task-line
  .task-list-label {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
  margin-inline-start: 0;
  /* The label is the box that participates in the line, so the shared optical
   * anchor has to go here — on the checkbox itself it is inert, the label's own
   * baseline alignment having already placed it. */
  vertical-align: middle;
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list.HyperMD-task-line
  .task-list-item-checkbox {
  /* Half its own width back from the column, so its centre lands on it. */
  margin-inline-start: calc(var(--checkbox-size) / -2);
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .list-bullet {
  width: 0;
  /* Dot-sized rather than line-height-tall, so `vertical-align: middle` has the
   * dot's own box to align and lands it on the same optical centre every
   * synthetic marker uses. Natively the box is the full line height and its
   * flex-centred `::after` therefore sits on the text RECT's centre, about
   * 1.4px below the optical one and ~5px below where a block marker sits —
   * the two-rules-for-one-column problem. */
  height: var(--list-bullet-size);
  vertical-align: middle;

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  margin-left: calc(var(--to-supp-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit)) !important;
}

/*
 * LIST GEOMETRY (lists-on-the-outline-grid, docs/research/16). Everything here
 * hangs off `to-decor-list`, a class the decoration puts on LIST-ITEM LINES
 * ONLY, so both gates — outline mode, and "lists only" — come from the
 * decoration itself and these rules need no second condition. Outline mode off
 * is untouched: no class, none of this.
 *
 * The approach is to set the variables Obsidian's own list layout reads rather
 * than to fight the boxes it produces. Measured (research doc, E1/E3):
 * `--list-indent` drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width` on each
 * `.cm-indent` span, so pushing our own unit into it retargets every list level
 * at once — one indent step for every kind, which is the whole change.
 *
 * `rem`, not the `em`-based value Obsidian ships: `--list-indent` resolves
 * where it is USED, so an `em` unit inflates on a heading's larger font — the
 * Experiment 1 bug, reachable through a new door.
 *
 * What this does NOT get for free is the hanging indent; see `--to-list-hang`
 * below.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-indent: var(--to-decor-unit);

  /* Our own gradient draws every list level now (`computeLineGuides` publishes
   * their depths and `activeGuideDepths` folds them in), so Obsidian's own line
   * would double up on the same column. Only its BORDER goes: the `.cm-indent`
   * spans still do the layout, and they exist only while the user's own "Show
   * indentation guides" setting is on — which stays the user's to set. */
  --indentation-guide-width: 0px;
  --indentation-guide-width-active: 0px;

  /* A bullet is a marker like any other: same weight, same colour token, so a
   * snippet retunes lists and blocks together. 0.38em against Obsidian's 0.30em
   * default — measured against the block icons' ink, which are 0.85rem at
   * stroke-width 1.5 in this same `--text-faint`. */
  --list-bullet-size: 0.38em;
}

/*
 * The marker's own column, and the text column one gutter right of it.
 *
 * Native rendering puts the bullet a `--list-indent-editing` gap right of the
 * item's column, where every other kind centres its marker ON the column. That
 * gap is what made a guide appear to run beside its bullet rather than out of
 * it. Zeroing the gap and sizing the whole marker SPAN to the gutter is what
 * makes the text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction,
 * rather than the sum of a padding, a glyph and a space.
 *
 * `min-width`, not `width`, so a wide ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own
 * text out instead of overlapping it — ordered markers therefore START on the
 * column rather than centring on it, which is the deliberate exclusion the
 * spec states.
 *
 * Task lines are excluded throughout: the checkbox lives in this same span, is
 * wider than the gutter, and is a real click target whose hit area is not this
 * layer's to reshape.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-padding-inline-start: 0px;

  /*
   * The hanging indent, STATED rather than read from Obsidian's own.
   *
   * `(depth − supplementalDepth)` is the item's depth within its own list, so
   * that many units is how far Obsidian's list rendering has already carried it
   * right of the line box; one gutter more is where its text begins. Wrapped
   * rows land exactly there.
   *
   * Obsidian computes this pair itself, from a live measurement, and gets it
   * wrong here twice over (both measured, research doc): the measurement takes
   * `coordsAtPos` at the end of the marker, which is the end of the marker's
   * TEXT rather than of its padded box, so with the span sized to the gutter
   * every wrapped row landed 16px left of its own item's text; and the value is
   * cached per line and invalidated only by a text change or a DOM mutation its
   * observer sees — `childList`, `characterData`, `subtree`, never attributes,
   * which is all a decoration changes — so turning outline mode on for an open
   * note left the old wrap column in place until a note switch.
   *
   * A stated value has neither problem, and needs no measurement of ours. The
   * `!important` is what beats Obsidian's own inline style; the same rule
   * `to-decor-block` already relies on.
   */
  --to-list-hang: calc(
    (var(--to-depth, 0) - var(--to-supp-depth, 0)) * var(--to-decor-unit) +
      var(--to-marker-gutter)
  );

  text-indent: calc(-1 * var(--to-list-hang)) !important;
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6

  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)

  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
}

/*
 * An ordered item's number is a node marker like any other, so it centres on
 * the column too. It cannot do that by shrinking its box the way a bullet does
 * — the glyphs ARE the mark, and their width is the font's and the number's —
 * so the box keeps its layout position (text stays at `column + gutter`) and
 * the painted glyphs are shifted half their own width left. `transform` is what
 * makes that free: it moves the ink without moving anything around it.
 *
 * The shift is half the GUTTER, not half the number's own width. Centring each
 * number on its own width was tried and measured: `1. ` centres exactly, but
 * `10. ` reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, and nothing is left
 * for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px on that side and cannot go further
 * without crossing the parent level's guide. A fixed shift centres a
 * single-digit marker exactly, leans wider ones right — into their own text's
 * space, which `min-width` has already accounted for — and gives every number
 * in a list ONE left edge, which reads as a column rather than as ragged
 * centring.
 */

  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)

}

/*
 * Obsidian's fold chevron on a list line renders with its right edge ON the
 * item's own content origin — which, now that a marker is CENTRED on the column
 * rather than starting right of it, is straight through that marker: measured,
 * the glyph occupies [column-10, column] while a bullet's dot occupies
 * [column-3, column+3].
 *
 * `--list-bullet-end-padding` looks like the lever and is not: raising it grows
 * the indicator's box to the right (its `inset-inline-end` compensates by
 * exactly as much), leaving the glyph where it was. Measured at 1.3rem, 2rem
 * and 2.6rem — the glyph stayed at [14, 24] in all three.
 *
 * So the glyph is moved directly. It is absolutely positioned, so a transform
 * moves the ink and disturbs no layout. Half a gutter clears the widest centred
 * mark (a checkbox, half of it 8px) and 2px more keeps it off the ordered
 * marker's own left edge, while staying clear of the parent level's guide one
 * unit away.
 */

  > .cm-line.to-decor-list

/* A zero-width bullet box centres its own `::after` — which is where the dot

 * `-`/`*`/`+` character inside is already transparent, so letting it overflow
 * costs nothing visually. */
/*
 * A task line's marker is a checkbox, not a bullet, but it is the same THING —
 * the mark that stands for the node — so it takes the same column, CENTRED on
 * it exactly as a bullet's dot is. Natively it starts 7.33px right of the
 * column (the label's own -4px and the input's own inline-start margin,
 * measured), which in a mixed list puts a checkbox visibly nearer its text than

 * centres it. `--checkbox-size` is Obsidian's own variable for that width, so

 * it is not — 16px against a 20px gutter — so there was never anything stopping

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6

  vertical-align: middle;

content.content:
overflow-x: auto !important;
  max-width: 100% !important;
}

/*
 * Fold-indicator/marker crowding (Experiment 5a follow-up): a heading's
 * native collapse chevron (`.cm-fold-indicator .collapse-indicator`) is
 * inserted at essentially the same "line start" position our own marker
 * icon anchors to, and its own `inset-inline-end: 0` (no extra offset)
 * lands it right on top of our marker at every heading level — confirmed
 * live via `document.styleSheets` inspection of the actual matching rule.
 *
 * A first attempt mirrored Obsidian's OWN list-line override for this same
 * problem (`padding-inline-end` + a matching negative `inset-inline-end`,
 * driven there by a `--list-bullet-end-padding` theme variable) — but
 * verified live (screenshot + rect measurement) that this widens the
 * chevron's own invisible hit-area rightward without actually relocating
 * the visible glyph — the two properties' effects on a shrink-to-fit
 * `position: absolute` flex box cancel out for the glyph's own position,
 * they don't move it. `transform: translateX()` instead moves the WHOLE
 * rendered box — glyph and hit-area together — unambiguously, confirmed
 * live to actually place the chevron to the left of our marker instead of
 * merely reducing the overlap.
 *
 * The shift is depth-independent by construction, the same way
 * `markerLeftShiftExpr` (decorations.ts) turned out to be: the chevron's
 * wrapper is inserted at essentially the same "text start" anchor our own
 * marker's target column is defined relative to, so the needed leftward
 * distance is always `gutter + half the marker's own width + a small
 * visual gap`, regardless of heading depth.
 *
 * A real spatial constraint, found via a real-vault report (a nested
 * heading, not this experiment's flat 2-level fixtures): for a heading at
 * depth N > 0, the guide column belonging to its shallowest ANCESTOR (not
 * its own depth) also passes through this line, one `--to-decor-unit`
 * closer to the marker than the shift above accounts for. Measured live at
 * depth 2: ~17px of clear space exists between that ancestor guide and the
 * marker's own left edge.
 *
 * A second real correction, also caught by manual review (not assumed from
 * the box model): the WRAPPER box (`.collapse-indicator`, 22px, what the
 * two paragraphs above size against) is NOT the same as the visible glyph —
 * confirmed live via the actual `<svg>` element's own rect and `<path>`
 * `getBBox()`: the painted glyph is only ~10px wide, centered inside that
 * 22px box (~6px of invisible padding on each side, part of the click
 * hit-area but never painted). The 17px gap comfortably fits a 10px glyph;
 * the earlier "22px can't fit in 17px" conclusion measured the wrong box.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='styles.css'
s=open(p).read()

# --- fix 2: ordered marker centres on the block icon's own left edge
old_ol = """ * The shift is half the GUTTER, not half the number's own width. Centring each
 * number on its own width was tried and measured: `1. ` centres exactly, but
 * `10. ` reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, and nothing is left
 * for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px on that side and cannot go further
 * without crossing the parent level's guide. A fixed shift centres a
 * single-digit marker exactly, leans wider ones right — into their own text's
 * space, which `min-width` has already accounted for — and gives every number
 * in a list ONE left edge, which reads as a column rather than as ragged
 * centring.
 */"""
new_ol = """ * The shift is a FIXED half-icon, not half the number's own width. Centring
 * each number on its own width was tried and measured: `1. ` centres exactly,
 * but `10. ` reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, and nothing is
 * left for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px on that side and cannot go
 * further without crossing the parent level's guide. A fixed shift gives every
 * number in a list ONE left edge, which reads as a column rather than as ragged
 * centring, and leans wider ones right into their own text's space, which
 * `min-width` has already accounted for.
 *
 * Half the MARKER ICON, so that left edge is the block icon's left edge: a
 * number and a paragraph's icon at the same depth then start together, which
 * is the comparison a reader actually makes when a numbered list sits above a
 * paragraph. Half the gutter was tried first and put the digits 3.2px further
 * left than the icon beside them — measured, and visible.
 */"""
assert old_ol in s
s = s.replace(old_ol, new_ol)

old = """  .cm-formatting-list-ol {
  transform: translateX(calc(var(--to-marker-gutter) / -2));
}"""
new = """  .cm-formatting-list-ol {
  transform: translateX(calc(var(--to-marker-icon-size, 0.85rem) / -2));
}"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)

# --- fix 1: chevron lands where a block's chevron lands
old_chev = """ * So the glyph is moved directly. It is absolutely positioned, so a transform
 * moves the ink and disturbs no layout. Half a gutter clears the widest centred
 * mark (a checkbox, half of it 8px) and 2px more keeps it off the ordered
 * marker's own left edge, while staying clear of the parent level's guide one
 * unit away.
 */"""
new_chev = """ * So the glyph is moved directly. It is absolutely positioned, so a transform
 * moves the ink and disturbs no layout.
 *
 * The distance is the block rule's, minus its gutter term. That rule (further
 * down this file) lands a block chevron's painted glyph with its right edge at
 * `column - icon/2 - 3px`: clear of the marker's own left edge by a 3px visual
 * gap. It needs the gutter because a block line's chevron is anchored at the
 * TEXT origin, one gutter right of the column; a list line's is anchored at its
 * content origin, which the rules above have already put ON the column. Drop
 * the gutter and the two kinds' chevrons land at the same offset from their own
 * marker — which is what a reader compares, a list item and a heading being
 * foldable side by side.
 *
 * Measured against half a gutter plus 2px, which this replaces: that put the
 * list chevron 2.2px further left than a heading's, close enough to the parent
 * level's guide to read as belonging to it rather than to its own marker.
 */"""
assert old_chev in s
s = s.replace(old_chev, new_chev)

old = """  .collapse-indicator {
  transform: translateX(calc(var(--to-marker-gutter) / -2 - 2px));
}"""
new = """  .collapse-indicator {
  transform: translateX(calc(-1 * (var(--to-marker-icon-size, 0.85rem) / 2 + 3px)));
}"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)

open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='styles.css'
s=open(p).read()
anchor = """.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .cm-formatting-list {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
}"""
assert anchor in s
block = """/*
 * The leading whitespace, sized to OUR depth instead of to what Obsidian made
 * of the characters.
 *
 * Obsidian wraps every list line's leading whitespace in one
 * `.cm-hmd-list-indent` span, and inside it quantises only what it recognises:
 * a tab or exactly four spaces becomes a `.cm-indent` of one `--list-indent`,
 * and whatever is left over stays a `.cm-indent-spacing` of literal space
 * glyphs. Measured, on a two-space-indented file: levels 1, 3 and 5 land on
 * columns and levels 2 and 4 land 8.38px right of the level above — the list
 * walks up the page at the font's space advance while our guides, drawn from
 * the parse, stay one unit apart. Every level is a level to the parse and to
 * reading mode; only the editor's whitespace arithmetic disagrees.
 *
 * Sizing the WRAPPER states the answer once, for whatever it contains: the
 * item's depth within its own list, in units. That covers the quantised part
 * and the leftover together, so a two-space file, a three-space file and a
 * six-space level all land where the parse says they are.
 *
 * It also removes this layer's dependence on the user's "Show indentation
 * guides" setting. Measured with it off: the `.cm-indent` spans are not emitted
 * at all, the wrapper holds raw text, and nothing is quantised — a FOUR-space
 * level then renders 7.25px left of its column. The wrapper is emitted either
 * way, so one rule covers both.
 *
 * `white-space: pre` and `overflow: hidden` keep whitespace wider than its own
 * box from wrapping the line or spilling over the marker; `vertical-align: top`
 * keeps an `overflow: hidden` inline-block — whose baseline would otherwise be
 * its bottom margin edge — from dropping the row it sits in.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list
  .cm-hmd-list-indent {
  display: inline-block;
  width: calc((var(--to-depth, 0) - var(--to-supp-depth, 0)) * var(--to-decor-unit));
  white-space: pre;
  overflow: hidden;
  vertical-align: top;
}

"""
s = s.replace(anchor, block + anchor)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')
PY

content.text:
Fixes 1, 2 and 4 are in [styles.css](styles.css) and measured exact. Fix 3 is previewed but not built — it needs a decision.

**1. Fold chevron.** The list rule shifted by a self-chosen `gutter/2 + 2px`. The block rule (further down the same file) lands a chevron's painted glyph at `column − icon/2 − 3px`; it needs the gutter term because a block's chevron anchors at the *text* origin, one gutter right of the column, while a list's anchors at its content origin — which these rules already put *on* the column. Dropping the gutter term makes them the same rule. Measured after: heading glyph right edge at `column − 9.8`, list glyph right edge at `column − 9.8`.

**2. Ordered number.** Was half a gutter (10px); now half the marker icon (6.8px), so a number's left edge *is* a block icon's left edge. Measured: ordered marker at 17.2, paragraph icon at 17.21, same depth.

**4. Space indentation — this was one rule, and bigger than two-space files.** Obsidian wraps a list line's whole leading whitespace in one `.cm-hmd-list-indent` span and quantises only tabs and exact four-space groups *inside* it; the remainder stays literal space glyphs, which is the drift you saw. Sizing that wrapper to `(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit` states the answer for whatever it contains. Two-space levels now measure 24/48/72/96/120; tabs unchanged; line heights and row counts unchanged.

It also closes a residual the proposal had recorded separately: with **"Show indentation guides" off**, Obsidian emits no `.cm-indent` at all, so even a *four-space* list was off grid (level 2 bullet at 40.75 instead of 48). Now identical either way.

**3. Task text — needs your call.** The space after `]` is the first character of the *content* span. On a bullet line the equivalent space sits *inside* `.cm-formatting-list`, which is min-width'd to the gutter and swallows it; on a task line it isn't, so the text starts one space advance (4.19px) further out. Worth correcting one measurement I made earlier: the *gap* is not actually larger on task lines — 17px bullet-to-text against 16.2px checkbox-to-text. What reads as larger is the text column being 4.2px further right than every other line's.

There's no CSS unit for a space advance (`ch` is the digit's, 9.6px here), so the exact fix is to measure it once per render into a custom property — the same pattern `--to-chevron-dead-right` already uses. The "after" screenshot shows it with the measured value injected. Want me to build it that way, or leave the 4px?

One thing you didn't flag but will see in the shot: `10. ordered ten`'s text starts 8px right of `1.`/`2.` — `min-width` pushing its own text out rather than overlapping it. That's the documented trade-off for wide ordered markers; say the word if it should change.

content.content:
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: One indentation grid for every kind

In outline mode, the distance between one tree level and the next SHALL be the same for every
kind, including list items. A list level SHALL step by the outline unit rather than by
Obsidian's own list-indent value, so that a node's rendered column is a function of its tree
depth alone and never of the kind that encodes it.

This SUPERSEDES the previous guarantee that a pure list renders byte-identical to
outline-mode-off. Byte-identity with stock Obsidian is now stated of outline mode OFF only:
with the mode off, every list — pure or not — SHALL render exactly as stock Obsidian renders
it, with no contribution from any decoration layer.

The grid SHALL be derived from a single unit value used by every layer that positions
anything: indentation, guides, markers, and any accent drawn on them. A layer SHALL NOT
compute a column from a second source.

Whether the SOURCE indentation of a list actually renders one unit per level is Obsidian's
own affair and is not guaranteed here: Obsidian resolves a tab or exactly four spaces into one
indent unit and renders anything shorter at its literal width. A document indented in units
Obsidian does not resolve renders its list levels at columns this requirement does not
control, with the mode on or off.

#### Scenario: A list level and a heading level are the same distance

- **WHEN** a document contains a heading three tree levels deep and a list item three tree
  levels deep, in a file indented with tabs
- **THEN** both render at the same column, and each level of the list is one unit from the
  last — the same unit that separates the heading levels

#### Scenario: Ordered lists and task lists take the same grid

- **WHEN** a nested ordered list and a nested task list are open in outline mode
- **THEN** each of their levels steps by the same unit as a bullet list's

#### Scenario: Outline mode off is stock

- **WHEN** outline mode is turned off on a note containing a nested list
- **THEN** every list line renders exactly as stock Obsidian renders it — the same columns,
  the same bullet, the same guides — with no decoration contribution of any kind

#### Scenario: A note open without outline mode is unaffected by one that has it

- **WHEN** one note with outline mode on and one without are open at the same time
- **THEN** the note without it renders its lists exactly as stock Obsidian does

### Requirement: Indentation is additive, and every kind takes the same grid
Every node's lines SHALL carry an indentation contribution equal to `depth × unit`,
computed from the node's distance from the document root in the parsed tree — not from raw
...
### Requirement: Markers and guides share one column definition

Every layer that positions something at a depth's column — the guide gradient, a marker's own
offset, and any accent drawn on either — SHALL derive that column from ONE definition, so no
two of them can be changed independently.

Every marker that stands for a node SHALL have its visible centre on that column, so the
visible centre of a guide line and the visible centre of the marker on it coincide. That is
every synthetic block marker, an unordered list item's native bullet, and a task item's
checkbox — a checkbox is the same kind of mark as a bullet and takes the column the same way,
whatever its own width. Its width and hit area SHALL NOT be changed to achieve that.

An ordered item's number is positioned by the same rule with one qualification, because its
mark IS its glyphs and their width is the font's and the number's: it SHALL be shifted onto the
column by a fixed amount — half the marker gutter — rather than by half its own width. A
number whose glyphs fit within the gutter therefore centres on the column, and a wider one
leans right of it into the space its own text already reserves — how wide "wide" is depends on
the font, so which numbers centre exactly is not fixed. Every number in a list SHALL share one
left edge, and none SHALL overlap its own item's text.

Shifting each number by half its OWN width is explicitly rejected: it centres every number but
reaches so far left that no fold chevron can fit beside it without crossing the parent level's
guide (measured, `100. ` reaches 19px left of its column against a parent guide 24px away).

A marker's VERTICAL placement SHALL follow one rule across kinds — including the two excluded
above: a marker SHALL sit at the same position relative to its own node's first text row
whatever the node's kind, so markers on adjacent rows read as one column.

#### Scenario: A bullet sits on its own guide, not beside it

- **WHEN** an unordered list item has children, so a guide descends from it through its subtree
- **THEN** the bullet's visible centre and the guide's visible centre are the same column

#### Scenario: A block marker and a bullet agree on the column

- **WHEN** a paragraph and an unordered list item at the same tree depth are visible in one
  document
- **THEN** their markers render on the same column, and their text starts at the same column
  one marker gutter further right

#### Scenario: A wide ordered marker starts on the column and pushes its own text

- **WHEN** an ordered list contains both single- and double-digit items
- **THEN** every marker starts at its own depth column, and the wider one pushes its own text
  right rather than overlapping it or crossing the column

#### Scenario: An ordered list's numbers share a left edge, with a single digit on the column

- **WHEN** an ordered list contains single- and multi-digit items
- **THEN** every number starts at the same column, half a gutter left of the depth column; a
  number narrow enough to fit the gutter is centred on that column; and no number overlaps its
  own item's text

#### Scenario: A fold chevron does not overlap the marker it belongs to

- **WHEN** a list item has children, so Obsidian renders its fold chevron
- **THEN** the chevron renders clear of that item's own marker, and clear of the parent level's
  guide column

#### Scenario: A checkbox and a bullet in one list share a column

- **WHEN** a list contains both task items and plain items
- **THEN** every marker's visible centre is on the same column, so no item's mark sits nearer
  its own text than its neighbours' do

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Indentation guides render every ancestor level, including list levels
Every line SHALL carry an indentation-guide decoration for each strict ancestor at a shallower
tree depth, whatever that ancestor's kind — a heading, paragraph or atom with descendants, and
a list item with descendants alike. Every line inside an ancestor's subtree renders that
ancestor's guide, on that ancestor's own depth column.

The plugin SHALL own this rendering rather than share it: wherever it draws a guide for a list
level it SHALL suppress Obsidian's own indent guide for that level, so exactly one line renders
per level. Guides SHALL render continuously through blank separator lines between sibling
blocks, not just through node content lines.

Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting SHALL remain the user's to set and SHALL NOT
be changed by the plugin; suppression SHALL be scoped to outline-mode list lines, leaving every
other context — other notes, reading view, the mode turned off — showing whatever that setting
asks for.

#### Scenario: A list's own nesting renders guides
- **WHEN** a list is nested several levels deep

content.content:
## Context

See proposal.md for motivation, and
[docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md](../../../docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md)
for the measurements every decision below rests on — taken live against Obsidian 1.13.4 in the
e2e harness, then reviewed by hand in a demo build whose two experimental settings this change
removes.

Four properties of Obsidian's own list rendering shape the approach, all confirmed live:

1. **`--list-indent` is a documented CSS variable** (`calc(--indent-unit × --indent-size)`,
   where `--indent-size` is the vault's Tab size) and drives exactly two things: `tab-size` on
   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.
2. **`.cm-indent` spans exist only while Obsidian's own "Show indentation guides" setting is
   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.
   Layout for space-indented files therefore depends on a setting the user owns, and on a
   quantum that is not the Tab size.
3. **The hanging indent is a cached live measurement** written as an inline style, invalidated
   on text change or on a DOM mutation Obsidian's own observer sees — `childList`,
   `characterData`, `subtree`, but not attributes.
4. **The variables must be overridden where they are USED, not on an intermediate holder.**
   `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
   overriding `--list-indent-editing` below it does nothing; overriding
   `--list-padding-inline-start` works. `--list-indent` is read directly by the line and its
   descendants and can be scoped as far down as a single `.cm-line`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
### D5 — Ordered markers start on the column; task checkboxes keep native geometry

`min-width`, not `width`, on the marker span: a bullet gets exactly the gutter and a wide
ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own text out rather than overlapping it. Ordered markers
therefore START on the column instead of centring on it, and an item numbered past 9 starts its
text slightly further right than its siblings. Right-aligning numbers into the gutter would
read better but needs a wrapper element the DOM does not provide.

A task checkbox is CENTRED on the column like a bullet, pulled back half its own width with
`margin-inline-start: calc(var(--checkbox-size) / -2)` — Obsidian's own variable for that
width, so a theme that resizes the control is followed rather than assumed away. Its width and
hit area are untouched.

Two earlier drafts of this decision were wrong, in opposite directions. The first said task
lines keep native geometry outright, which contradicted the requirement it was meant to
implement. The second brought the checkbox's START onto the column but excluded it from
centring, justified as "the checkbox is wider than the gutter" — measured, it is not: 16px
against a 20px gutter. Nothing was stopping it centring, and starting it there is exactly what
real use reported, a checkbox sitting nearer its text than the bullets above and below it in a
mixed list.

An ordered number takes the column too, with one qualification. Its mark IS its glyphs, so it
cannot shrink its box the way a bullet does; instead the painted glyphs are shifted left by a
fixed half-gutter with `transform`, which moves the ink without moving the box its own text
follows. A number whose glyphs fit inside the gutter therefore centres on the column, wider
ones lean right into the space `min-width` already reserves, and every number in a list shares
one left edge. Which numbers centre exactly is the font's business — `1. ` measures 18.4px in
the bundled theme on macOS and 20.36px on CI's Linux font, so the lean starts one digit earlier
there. The rule is the fixed shift; the centring is its consequence.

Shifting each number by half its OWN width was built first and measured out: it centres them
all, but `10. ` then reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, leaving nothing for the
fold chevron, which needs about 10px on that side and cannot go further without crossing the
parent level's guide one unit away.

### D8 — The fold chevron moves off the marker

Obsidian renders a list line's fold chevron with its right edge on the item's content origin.
That was harmless while a marker began to the RIGHT of that origin; now that markers are
centred ON it, the chevron sits straight through them — measured, the glyph occupies
`[column − 10, column]` while a bullet's dot occupies `[column − 3, column + 3]`.

`--list-bullet-end-padding` is the obvious lever and does nothing: raising it grows the
indicator's box to the right while its own `inset-inline-end` compensates by the same amount,
so the glyph does not move. Measured at 1.3rem, 2rem and 2.6rem — the glyph stayed put in all
three. So the glyph is translated directly; it is absolutely positioned, so nothing else moves.
Half a gutter clears the widest centred mark (a checkbox, half of it 8px) and two pixels more

   a list line, and `min-width` on each `.cm-indent` span. Setting it retargets every list
   level at once. Minimal, the most-installed community theme, already does this.

   on**, and one span is emitted per tab or per exactly four spaces — never per two or three.

content.content:
- Any note, not a special mode: the outliner isn't a separate note type or a vault takeover, it's a way of looking at and editing the notes you already have.
- Public APIs only: built on Obsidian's documented editor and plugin APIs, no monkey-patching private internals, so it stays compatible and passes the community plugin safety bar honestly.
- Clean files: no required front matter, IDs, or metadata just to make the outliner work. What the outliner needs to track (like fold state) lives in plugin data, not in your notes.

## Known limitations

- **List indentation must be tabs or four spaces.** Obsidian resolves a tab, or exactly four
  spaces, into one indent unit and renders anything shorter at its literal character width —
  with this plugin disabled too. Outline mode puts every list level on one grid by supplying
  that unit, so a file indented two or three spaces keeps Obsidian's own uneven columns while
  the guides beside it are evenly spaced, which makes the mismatch easier to see rather than
  harder. Re-indenting such a file with tabs is the fix today.
- **Space-indented lists depend on Obsidian's "Show indentation guides" setting.** The spans
  that carry a space-indented list's layout only exist while it is on. Tab-indented lists are
  unaffected. The plugin never changes that setting.

## Approach

- The design splits into two layers:
  - A pure mapping core: markdown parsing, encoding, and structural operations (indent, outdent, move, etc.) as a standalone library with no editor or Obsidian dependency. Correctness here (round-tripping, op closure, minimal edits) is verified independently of any UI.
  - An editor integration: a CodeMirror 6 extension inside Obsidian's standard markdown view that renders and drives that model, giving the outliner experience without replacing the file format or the editor.
- The mapping algebra has two structural regimes:
  - Headings behave like org-mode promote/demote: indent/outdent shifts heading level.
  - Everything else reparents relative to siblings, with markdown encoding recomputed from context.
  - Either way, an operation produces a well-formed tree, or it's rejected with a clear, typed reason, never a partial or ambiguous result.
- The research and design decisions behind these choices are written up in [docs/research/](docs/research/).

### Phase 4 — indentation Obsidian does not quantize (experiment)

Only reached if phases 1–3 leave it worth solving. Three candidates:

- A per-line `--to-list-level` from `Decoration.line` plus an explicit width on
  `.cm-hmd-list-indent`. Geometry, caret round-trip and click mapping all measured correct;
  the open question is whether Obsidian's hang measurement sees our width on the first render
  (the probe applied the level after render, which is exactly the case that fails).
- A `Decoration.replace` widget standing in for the whitespace. Structurally the cleanest —
  Obsidian would measure our widget as ordinary content — and the only fully unvalidated
  mechanism here. Needs a spike in the plugin, not a page-level probe.
- A document-level "normalize list indentation" command. Not a decoration at all, but this
  project already rewrites list indentation on every structural operation, so a one-shot
  normalizer is consistent with the model and removes the problem at the source.

## Carried-forward findings

For [11-decoration-lessons.md](11-decoration-lessons.md) when this work lands:

- **Look for the variable before building the mechanism.** Two prior probes concluded that
  list columns could only be followed by measurement. They were measuring the right thing and
  asking the wrong question: the columns are computed from public CSS variables, so they can
  be *set* instead of followed. The cost of the wrong question was a deferred feature and a
  planned second rendering mechanism.
- **Override the variable that the rule using it reads, not an intermediate one.**
  `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared on
  `.markdown-source-view`; overriding `--list-indent-editing` further down the tree does
  nothing, because the substitution already happened above. Overriding
  `--list-padding-inline-start` itself works. `--list-indent` is consumed directly by
  `.cm-line`/`.cm-indent` and can be scoped as far down as our own per-line class.
- **Obsidian's list hanging-indent is a cached live measurement, and its cache does not watch
  attributes.** Anything that changes the rendered width of a list prefix through CSS alone
  leaves the hang stale until the line's text changes or the view is rebuilt. Changing the
  rendered width through a variable that is already in effect at first render is the way to
  avoid the problem rather than fight it.
- **`--list-indent` is `em`-based.** Any of our own values that flow into it must be `rem`, or
  the Experiment-1 font-size bug returns through a new door.
- **A user setting can move geometry.** "Show indentation guides" does not only paint: with it
  off, the `.cm-indent` spans do not exist, and space-indented list levels change width. Any
  reasoning about list columns has to name which side of that setting it holds on.

## Native chrome: retargeting rather than replacing

Findings from `lists-on-the-outline-grid` (measurements:
[16-native-list-decoration.md](16-native-list-decoration.md)).

- **Look for the variable before building the mechanism.** Two probes concluded that native
  list columns could only be FOLLOWED, by per-item pixel measurement, and planned a second
  rendering mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient. They were measuring the right
  thing and asking the wrong question: the columns are computed from public CSS variables, so
  they can be SET. The cost of the wrong question was a deferred feature and a planned overlay
  layer that turned out to be unnecessary.
- **Override the variable the consuming rule reads, not an intermediate one.**
  `--list-padding-inline-start: var(--list-indent-editing)` is declared high in the tree, so
  overriding `--list-indent-editing` further down does nothing — the substitution already
  happened above. Overriding `--list-padding-inline-start` itself works. `--list-indent` is
  consumed directly by `.cm-line`/`.cm-indent` and can be scoped as far down as a single line's
  own class, which is what gates all of this on outline mode with no second condition.
- **Obsidian's list hanging indent is a cached live measurement, and its cache does not watch
  attributes.** It observes `childList`, `characterData` and `subtree`, so anything that
  changes the rendered width of a list prefix through CSS alone leaves the hang stale until the
  line's text changes or the view is rebuilt. It also measures `coordsAtPos` at the end of the
  marker, which is the end of the marker's TEXT rather than of its padded box. Both are reasons
  to STATE a value the layer already knows instead of reading one back.
- **`--list-indent` is `em`-based.** Anything of ours flowing into it must be `rem`, or the
  Experiment 1 font-size bug returns through a new door.
- **A user setting can move geometry, not just paint.** With Obsidian's "Show indentation
  guides" off, the `.cm-indent` spans do not exist at all, and space-indented list levels
  change width. Any reasoning about list columns has to name which side of that setting it
  holds on.
- **`vertical-align: middle` resolves against the PARENT's x-height, which makes it
  font-size-relative in a way that bites on headings.** It is the right optical anchor for a
  small mark beside body text and the wrong one for a marker on an H1, where it drops the mark
  below the heading's own glyphs. Two marks of different size and box model may simply not
  share one numeric vertical anchor; that is worth discovering by looking rather than asserting
  in a spec.

## Verification and process discipline

- **The synthetic corpus, even a deliberately adversarial one, missed all three real bugs
  above.** Every one was caught only by a tester visually reviewing real, organic vault
  content (not synthetic fixtures, not DOM-attribute assertions). This reaffirms the
  postmortem's central lesson directly, in a new implementation: treat the real-vault pass
  as load-bearing verification for every future experiment, not a final formality after the
  fixtures pass.
- **A script-driven interaction (setting `.scrollLeft` programmatically, reading it back) is
  real evidence that a scroll container is *functional*, but it is not equivalent to a user
  actually using it.** It doesn't exercise trackpad/wheel gesture handling, doesn't reveal
  whether a scrollbar is visually discoverable, and doesn't catch problems that only show up
  under real input events. A fix that passes every computed-style and scripted-interaction
  check should still be handed to a tester for a final pass before being called settled if the
  thing being fixed is itself a user-facing interaction (as opposed to, say, a purely visual
  property like a color or an alignment, where a computed-style check IS the full story).
- **Consolidating a fix from a scratch/probe test into the "real" file is itself a step that

content.content:
## 7. Interaction with `lists-on-the-outline-grid`

That change pushes `--to-decor-unit` into Obsidian's `--list-indent` and puts a list marker on
its own depth column, so every kind's marker centre sits at `depth × unit`. Three consequences
for this question:

1. **Aligned markers become the grid's statement that two nodes are siblings.** Under readings C
   and D, a flush list after a paragraph would render with its bullet on the paragraph's column.
   That is not an anomaly to correct — it is what siblinghood means once kind no longer affects
   x-position.
2. **Special extra indentation for top-level list items would be a regression.** It would put
   kind back into the x-position, which is the exact defect the grid change exists to remove.
3. **Today's rule masks the question.** Because a list after a paragraph is currently a child, it
   renders one unit deeper and coincidentally matches the intuition that lists sit right of
   prose. Changing the reading makes that alignment literal, and the grid is what makes it
   legible rather than strange.

**Sequencing: the grid change lands first.** Its verification gate covers tab / four-space /
two-space, ordered, task and wrapping fixtures, and a mapping change moves depths in exactly the
mixed documents those fixtures use. Doing the mapping first invalidates the fixtures mid-flight;
doing it after gives the new depths a settled reference to be judged against.

## 8. What is decided, and what is not

**Decided:** a reorder refuses the arrangement it cannot encode (`reorder-absorption`). That
change touches no mapping rule and no encoding path. It is written to be deleted: under readings
C and D its predicate never fires.

**Not decided:** the reading. Nothing here commits the project to A, C or D. B is ruled out on
§6, and should not be reopened without new information about Obsidian's indent quantization.

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix(decorations): four things a manual pass saw that the fixtures did not

A real-vault review of the list grid reported four visual defects. Each turned
out to be a placement chosen independently of the one beside it, or a width
accepted from Obsidian instead of stated.

Space-indented lists were off the grid (design D9). Setting `--list-indent`
retargets the levels Obsidian RESOLVES; it does nothing for the ones it does
not. Obsidian quantises a tab or exactly four spaces and renders the remainder
at the font's space advance, so a two-space file walked right a fraction of a
level at a time — measured at unit 24px: levels 1, 3 and 5 on their columns,
levels 2 and 4 8.38px off — while our guides stayed a unit apart, putting the
bullets ON them. Both halves share one `.cm-hmd-list-indent` wrapper, so sizing
that wrapper to `(depth - supplementalDepth) x unit` states the answer for
whatever is inside it, from the two properties the hanging indent already
publishes. This also retires the residual about Obsidian's own "Show
indentation guides" setting: with it off nothing is quantised at all and even a
FOUR-space level rendered 7.25px short, and the wrapper is emitted either way.
Both residuals had been accepted and documented; one rule removed them, so the
README's "Known limitations" section and the demo note's "Known limitation"
section go with them.

A task item's text started 4.19px right of every other kind's (design D10).
Obsidian leaves the space after `]` as the first character of the CONTENT span,
where the marker span's `min-width` cannot absorb it the way it absorbs a
bullet's. The label is sized one space short of the gutter instead. Worth
recording that the first reading of the report was wrong: the marker-to-text
GAP is not larger on a task line (17px on a bullet against 16.2px on a task) —
it is the text COLUMN that is out. No CSS unit expresses a space's advance, so
it is measured live into `--to-space-advance`, same pattern and same reasons as
`--to-chevron-dead-right`.

An ordered number hung 3.2px left of the block icon beside it (design D5). The
fixed shift that gives every number one left edge is now half a MARKER ICON
rather than half a gutter, so that edge is the one a block marker at the same
depth begins at — the comparison a reader makes when a numbered list sits above
a paragraph.

A list's fold chevron sat 2.2px left of where a heading's sits (design D8),

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- One unit, one column definition, one guide mechanism, one marker rule — for every kind.
- No new rendering mechanism. Everything below is either a CSS variable Obsidian already reads
  or the gradient/`Decoration.line` machinery the layer already runs.
- No pixel measurement added. The layer keeps its measurement-free character; the one place a
  measurement exists today (Obsidian's hanging indent) is replaced by a stated value, not by
  one of ours.

**Non-Goals:**

- Rewriting a document's indentation to a canonical unit. This layer renders; it does not
  edit. A "normalize list indentation" command would be a structural-operations change.
- Making list rendering correct for files Obsidian itself does not quantise (two- and
  three-space indentation). See Risks.
- Turning the unit into a user setting. It becomes a single declared value so `--list-indent`
  can read it, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider
  layer-configurability item in `docs/research/12`.

=== D6a ===
### D6a — The vertical anchor stays per-kind (revised during implementation)

D6 said the vertical rule would be unified along with the horizontal one. The horizontal half
landed; the vertical half was built, looked at, and reversed.

`vertical-align: middle` is the optical centre of a row of lowercase text and is exactly right
for a bullet — it moved the dot the ~1.4px down that the review had reported as "a tad too
high". Applied to a synthetic marker it is wrong, because `middle` resolves against the
PARENT's x-height and a heading's parent is the heading: on an H1 the icon moved from 8.45px
above its text-rect centre to 2.96px BELOW it, landing under the heading's own glyphs and hard
against the guide that starts on the row beneath. Reported from the demo build as "icon
markers too low and overlapping the guides", and confirmed in a screenshot.

So the bullet keeps the optical anchor and the synthetic marker keeps `baseline`. They differ
by about 7px on a body-sized row. That is a real design finding rather than an unfinished
task: a 13.6px outline glyph in the text flow and a 6px dot in a flex box do not read as
aligned at one numeric offset, and no single CSS anchor serves both across font sizes. The
requirement was amended to say so rather than left stating something the implementation does
not do.

A task checkbox lands 0.46px off the bullet's anchor — the label is the box that participates
in the line and is taller than the control inside it. Left as measured.

### D7 — Remove the settings

input.description: Read the vertical-placement requirement text

content.content:
marker's own width, so an ordered number and a block marker at the same depth begin on the same
left edge — the comparison a reader makes when a numbered list sits above or below a paragraph.
Every number in a list SHALL therefore share one left edge; a number wider than the gutter
leans right into the space its own text already reserves; and none SHALL overlap its own item's
text.

Shifting each number by half its OWN width is explicitly rejected: it centres every number but
reaches so far left that no fold chevron can fit beside it without crossing the parent level's
guide (measured, `100. ` reaches 19px left of its column against a parent guide 24px away).

A marker's VERTICAL placement SHALL follow one rule across kinds — including the two excluded
above: a marker SHALL sit at the same position relative to its own node's first text row
whatever the node's kind, so markers on adjacent rows read as one column.

#### Scenario: A bullet sits on its own guide, not beside it

- **WHEN** an unordered list item has children, so a guide descends from it through its subtree
- **THEN** the bullet's visible centre and the guide's visible centre are the same column

#### Scenario: A block marker and a bullet agree on the column

- **WHEN** a paragraph and an unordered list item at the same tree depth are visible in one
  document
- **THEN** their markers render on the same column, and their text starts at the same column
  one marker gutter further right

#### Scenario: A wide ordered marker starts on the column and pushes its own text

- **WHEN** an ordered list contains both single- and double-digit items
- **THEN** every marker starts at its own depth column, and the wider one pushes its own text
  right rather than overlapping it or crossing the column
=== vertical scenarios ===

=== follow-up entry ===
### A list item's continuation line does not align with the item's own content

Two separate stock-Obsidian offsets, found while closing the row above and confirmed
byte-identical with outline mode **off** — neither is this plugin's to cause or to fix.

Obsidian wraps a continuation line's leading whitespace in `<span class="cm-hmd-list-indent
cm-hmd-list-indent-N">` and gives that span its own width. That width is derived from the
whitespace, not from the width of the MARKER the continuation is supposed to sit under, and
the two disagree:

| Line | Marker's own width | Continuation indent span | Continuation sits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `- alpha` | 23.42px | 24.38px | 0.96px right |
| `1. alpha` | 30.39px | 28.56px | **1.82px left** |
| `10. alpha` | 40.16px | 36.00px | **4.16px left** |

So an ordered list's continuation hangs slightly LEFT of its own text, worse the wider the
number — reported from real-vault use during the `decorate-provisional-positions` pass, where
it was visible on the newly-decorated provisional line and then found to predate it.

The second offset is about the CARET rather than the text, and appears only once the run
spans more than one nesting level: at end-of-line CM6 measures the caret by the text run's own

takes `hang - that`.

This also closes `docs/research/12`'s "a list item's continuation line does not
align with the item's own content", open since `decorate-provisional-positions`
and diagnosed as unclosable because it "would mean overriding the width of
`.cm-hmd-list-indent` … from a live measurement of the marker beside it". The
override is the same one; the measurement is unnecessary because the column is
stated rather than followed. Measured before the rule existed: 4.38px right of

pushes its own first row out and its continuation follows the grid's text column

Two capabilities change, both deliberately:

- `outline-decorations` — **"a pure list renders byte-identical to outline-mode-off" is removed.** That invariant was chosen when the layer deferred all list geometry to Obsidian, and it is precisely what kept lists off the grid. The half that protects users is kept and restated: outline mode **off** renders exactly as stock Obsidian, for a pure list and for every other document. Nothing on disk changes either way — this was a rendering guarantee only.
- `hierarchy-position-indicators` — "Trail rendering through list nesting uses native list chrome or is omitted" is replaced. The omission existed because list levels had no column this plugin could address.

## What this PR contains

Planning and the reviewed demo. **The implementation follows.**

- `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` — the measurements, the prior art (obsidian-outliner, Minimal, the community threading snippets), the rejected alternatives, and the residuals.
- `openspec/changes/lists-on-the-outline-grid/` — proposal, two delta specs, design, tasks. `openspec validate --strict` passes.
- The demo build itself, behind `listLayout` and `listBullet` settings that default to today's rendering, plus `test-vault/Notes/List decoration demo.md` as the review fixture. Task group 4 removes both settings; the demo stays until then so the comparison remains available while implementing.

## Rejected alternatives, both built and measured

- **Measured overlays at native list columns** (obsidian-outliner's technique, and Experiment 2a's) — a second rendering mechanism with its own reflow bookkeeping, which Experiment 2b exists to avoid.
- **A DOM nudge to invalidate Obsidian's hang cache** — appending an empty hidden span to each list line and removing it works, with the document byte-identical across the nudge. Backed out: this repo's own lint rule forbids DOM insertion into a plain `.cm-line` after a confirmed 100%-CPU mutation-observer feedback loop, and "the removal is synchronous so the loop cannot start" is a judgement, not a measurement. Stating the hang removes the need.

## Known residuals, recorded not fixed

- **Two- and three-space indented files.** Obsidian resolves only a tab or exactly four spaces into an indent unit, so those files are misaligned with the plugin disabled too — and our even guides make the mismatch more visible, not less. The durable fix is a normalize-indentation command, which is a structural-operations change.
- **Space-indented files depend on the user's "Show indentation guides" setting**, which controls whether the spans carrying list layout exist at all. Tab-indented files are unaffected.
- **Task checkboxes and wide ordered markers keep native geometry.** A checkbox lives in the marker span, is wider than the gutter, and is a real click target; right-aligning ordered numbers into the gutter needs a wrapper the DOM does not provide.
- **The indent unit does not become a user setting here** — it becomes a single declared value, which is the prerequisite; exposing it belongs with the wider layer-configurability item.

Unit tests, lint, typecheck and the full desktop e2e suite are green on this branch. The change's own gate is task group 6: geometry assertions across tab / four-space / two-space, ordered, task and wrapping fixtures; the full corpus screenshotted in both bundled themes; a manual pass with Minimal installed (it sets `--list-indent` itself and puts its own margin on list lines); and a real-vault pass by hand — which is where every bug in this layer's history was actually found.

content.content:
48 /tmp/pr-body.md
Puts list decoration on the same grid as everything else outline mode draws.

Today a document in outline mode has two layouts in it. Headings, paragraphs and atoms sit on a depth column every `--to-decor-unit`, with a marker centred on that column and a guide descending from it. Lists are handed back to Obsidian: a list level steps `2.25em` where every other level steps `1.5rem`, its guides sit on native columns our grid never touches, and a list ancestor gets no caret trail at all because there is no column of ours to draw one on.

The experiment series left it that way deliberately, and two later probes concluded native list columns could only be *followed*, by per-item pixel measurement — a second rendering mechanism alongside the measurement-free gradient the layer rests on. That was right about the mechanism it examined and wrong about the problem. Obsidian computes list columns from public CSS variables, so they can be **set**. `docs/research/16-native-list-decoration.md` measures the whole surface against a running Obsidian 1.13.4; a demo build of it was reviewed by hand and accepted.

## What the change does

- **One indentation grid for every kind.** `--to-decor-unit` is pushed into Obsidian's own `--list-indent` on outline-mode list lines, so a list level and a heading level are the same distance.
- **Our own guides draw every list level**, in the same gradient, colour and column a heading's guide uses. Obsidian's own list guide is suppressed on those lines — its width, never the user's "Show indentation guides" setting.
- **The caret trail reaches into lists.** With list levels on the grid, `computePositionTrail`'s two `isListItem` exclusions come out and the position indicator accents list levels like any other. This closes the omission `hierarchy-position-indicators` currently states as a requirement.
- **A list marker sits on its own depth column**, with the item's text at the marker gutter, so a guide descends *out of* its bullet rather than beside it.
- **We state the hanging indent instead of reading Obsidian's.** Measured: the marker gutter makes every soft-wrapped list row land 16px left of its own item's text, because `coordsAtPos` — and therefore Obsidian's own measurement — reports the end of the marker's *text*, not the end of its padded box. Writing the pair from `(depth − supplementalDepth) × unit + gutter` is exact, and being a `calc()` it also removes the stale-cache defect where retargeting the grid at runtime left the old wrap column in place.

All seven addressed, replied to, and resolved. Pushed as `cdef859`.

**The one that mattered:** the continuation-line comment was a real regression I'd introduced. Continuation lines carry `to-decor-list` too, so the wrapper rule sized them like first lines and put every continuation on the **marker's** column — 20px left of the row above it. The whole decorations group passed over it because the geometry suite only ever measured marker-bearing first lines. A first line spends the gutter on its native marker; a continuation has none and belongs under the item's text, so it takes the whole hang. `hasNativeMarker` already meant exactly "list-item first line" and had been sitting unused.

That fix also closed [docs/research/12](docs/research/12-decoration-follow-ups.md)'s long-open "a list item's continuation line does not align with the item's own content" — which had been written off as unclosable because it "would mean overriding the width of `.cm-hmd-list-indent` … from a live measurement of the marker beside it". Same override; the measurement isn't needed because the column is stated. Measured before: 4.38px right under a bullet, 8.56px right under `1. `. After: exact.

**The rest were documentation drift**, mostly from D6a — the vertical-anchor reversal from earlier in the branch. D6a claimed "the requirement was amended to say so"; it never was, so the delta spec still mandated one anchor across kinds while the CSS deliberately used two. Same correction propagated to the proposal and to task 1.2. Also: the "no pixel measurement added" goal predated `measureSpaceAdvance`, the "files Obsidian doesn't quantise" non-goal is what D9 does, and the setting-matrix test covered 4 of 9 combinations while claiming all.

Two things to flag:

- **A suite run reverted your scratch edits in the demo note** (`dlkfj`, the ordered list, the deep `lskjf` nesting). I restored them from a copy I'd saved — they're back in the working tree, uncommitted.
- **One local e2e failure**, the nested table-cell Mod-A test in the selection group. It passes in isolation and on a group re-run, and it's the same load-related flake family as before. Not claiming the full-suite run as clean: it was 21/22 with that one.

Pushed as `82744fa`.

Same font trap, fourth time — and the first since I put the warning in that file's header, which is worth saying plainly: I wrote the header and then violated it in the next test I added.

**What failed:** `1. one`'s own first row is at 44.36 on CI, its continuation at 44. The rendering is right — that 0.36px *is* the wide-marker exception I'd documented two commits earlier. `1. ` is 20.36px on CI's Linux font against 18.4px on macOS, so where the gutter is 20px the marker's `min-width` pushes its own first row out while the continuation stays on the grid's text column. Locally the marker fits, so equality held and the test passed.

**The fix:** assert what the rule states — a continuation's text is one gutter right of its own depth column, for every kind, and its item's first row is never left of it. That still fails by the full 20px with the `--to-list-marker-cols` term removed, so it guards the same regression.

The general warning in the header wasn't specific enough to stop me. It now names the actual trap: an ordered item's own text column is not a fixed offset from anything and must never appear on either side of an equality — not against another kind's text column, not against its own continuation's. I sharpened the memory the same way, and audited the other 18 `textX` assertions in the file: the rest are either bounds (`>=`, `<`) or offsets from a column, which hold on any font.

own centre. The chevron's placement SHALL follow the mark rather than the line, since the mark
is what the reader relates it to.

A marker's VERTICAL placement is NOT unified across kinds, and that is a decision rather than
an omission."""

open(p,'w').write(s)

p='openspec/changes/lists-on-the-outline-grid/design.md'
s=open(p).read()
old = """A self-chosen half-gutter-plus-2px was built first and reviewed by hand: 2.2px further left

`56-list-grid.e2e.ts`, rather than each being checked against a distance of its own."""
new = """A self-chosen half-gutter-plus-2px was built first and reviewed by hand: 2.2px further left
than a heading's, close enough to the parent level's guide to read as belonging to that guide
rather than to its own marker. The two chevrons agreeing is now asserted as such in
`56-list-grid.e2e.ts`, rather than each being checked against a distance of its own.

**The vertical half is measured per line.** Obsidian centres `.collapse-indicator` on the line's
CONTENT BOX (`position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; align-items: center`), while every marker
kind takes its own vertical anchor — which D6a establishes cannot be unified. The two therefore
disagree by an amount that varies with kind AND font size: measured, +2.67px on an H1, +1.67 on
an H2, −0.80 on a paragraph, +1.78 on a bullet, +2.25 on a checkbox. No CSS expression produces
that set. A curve fitted to font size gets within ~0.2px and would be a constant for one theme
rather than a rule, so it is measured — for the few lines that have a chevron at all, reads
batched ahead of writes, unchanged lines not rewritten.

The measurement adds back whatever offset is currently applied, which is what makes it converge
rather than oscillate: a vertical POSITION, unlike the width difference `measureChevron` takes,
is not translation-invariant, so measuring an already-transformed chevron and writing the raw
difference would flip sign every render.

An ordered item is the one kind left without an offset. Its mark IS its glyphs, and no element's
box is where they sit: `.cm-formatting-list-ol`'s box is the text row, whose centre the chevron
already shares, while the digits rest on the baseline about 1.7px lower — where the bullet
beside them sits. Reading ink out of a text run needs font metrics no rect exposes. Anchoring to
the span would state a number that is not the mark's centre, so nothing is stated; recorded as a
follow-up in `docs/research/12`.

### D8a — Measure a value from the kind of element the rule consuming it applies to

`--to-chevron-dead-right` is measured from one representative chevron per render and consumed by
the BLOCK chevron rule. The query took the first `.cm-fold-indicator .collapse-indicator` in the
content DOM, of any kind — and the wrapper's width turns out to be a property of the LINE, not
of the chevron: measured, 15px on a heading or paragraph, 30.8px on a list item (widened by
`--list-bullet-end-padding`), 10px on a task line.

So the published value was whichever kind the rendered viewport happened to start with, and a
list item's 20.8px of dead space turns the block transform from −23.8px into −9px: every
heading's chevron jumps about 15px right, onto its own marker. Reported from real use as an
intermittent glitch that scrolling or folding could trigger and that reopening the note cleared
— the signature of a viewport-order dependency, since CM6 renders only the viewport and a fresh
view starts the cache empty.

The fix is one selector: measure from `.cm-line.to-decor-block`, the same kind the rule applies
to. The general form is worth stating, because this measurement pattern is used in three places
here: a representative measurement is only representative of the population the consuming rule
covers, so the query and the rule must name the same one. Nothing warned about it — the value
had a plausible fallback, the wrong value still rendered a chevron somewhere, and the fixture
corpus happened to put a heading first in every note.

reopening the note (a fresh view, empty cache, heading first).

docs/research/11 — a representative measurement is only representative of the
population its rule covers, and this pattern is used in three places here.

`.collapse-indicator` on the line's CONTENT BOX, while each marker kind takes
